name: Prime Minister's Employment Generation Programme (PMEGP)
ministry: Ministry of Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises

general_rural.note: General category gets 25% in rural areas (15% in urban, the base rate).

special_category_urban.note: SC/ST/OBC/Women/Minorities get 25% in urban areas (35% in rural).

special_category_rural.note: SC/ST/OBC/Women/Minorities get 35% in rural areas (25% in urban).

effective_interest_rate_note: Normal bank interest rate (11%-12%) applies, but the margin money subsidy reduces the principal amount you actually repay.
eligibility_human: Any individual above 18 years setting up a new unit. 8th standard pass is required only for manufacturing projects above ₹10 lakh or service projects above ₹5 lakh. Existing units or those who have already availed other govt subsidies are ineligible.
pros: Massive upfront capital subsidy up to 35% of project cost.
Maximum eligible project cost for manufacturing is ₹50 lakh and ₹20 lakh for the service sector.
cons: Strictly for new units; existing businesses cannot apply.
Subsidy is locked in a Term Deposit Receipt (TDR) for 3 years before it is fully adjusted.
application_steps: Submit application and DPR online via KVIC e-portal.
Application is routed to the selected bank branch.
Bank sanctions 90–95% of the project cost as a term loan.
Applicant deposits their 5–10% contribution.
KVIC routes the Margin Money (subsidy) to the bank, which is kept in a 3-year TDR.

name: PM Vishwakarma Scheme
ministry: Ministry of Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises / MSDE

toolkit_incentive.note: Up to ₹15,000 as an e-voucher to buy modern tools after basic training.

effective_interest_rate_note: Borrower pays a fixed 5% concessional interest rate; the government pays an 8% interest subvention directly to the bank.
eligibility_human: Self-employed artisans in the unorganized sector aged 18+ working in one of 18 specific traditional family-based trades (e.g., Carpenter, Blacksmith, Barber, Tailor). Cannot have taken similar govt loans (PMEGP, Mudra, SVANidhi) in the last 5 years.

documents_required.name: Active Mobile Number linked to Aadhaar

pros: Collateral-free Enterprise Development Loans up to ₹3 lakh in two tranches (₹1 lakh first, then ₹2 lakh) at a 5% fixed rate.
Paid skill training (Basic & Advanced) with a stipend of ₹500 per day.
Incentive of ₹1 per eligible digital transaction (up to 100/month).
cons: Restricted to only 18 specific traditional trades.
Only one member per family can register for the scheme benefits.
application_steps: Visit nearest Common Service Centre (CSC) with Aadhaar and complete e-KYC biometric authentication.
Application is vetted by local body, district committee, and screening committee.
Receive PM Vishwakarma Certificate & ID Card, then complete 5-7 days Basic Training.
Receive toolkit e-voucher (up to ₹15,000) and apply for the first loan tranche of ₹1 lakh.

name: Pradhan Mantri Mudra Yojana (PMMY) – Shishu
ministry: Ministry of Finance
effective_interest_rate_note: Ranges from 7.3% to 12% depending on the lending institution's MCLR; strictly collateral-free.
eligibility_human: Any Indian citizen looking for a small loan up to ₹50,000 to start or expand a non-corporate, non-farm income-generating activity.

documents_required.name: Quotation of Machinery/Items to be purchased

pros: Completely collateral-free with no processing fee for the Shishu tier.
Accessible through virtually all scheduled commercial banks and NBFCs.
cons: No direct capital subsidy component.
Approval rates heavily depend on the local branch manager's assessment of business viability.
application_steps: Prepare a simple one-page business plan or list of requirements.
Approach a local bank branch or apply online via the Udyamimitra portal.
Submit the simplified Shishu application form along with quotations.

name: PM SVANidhi (Street Vendor's AtmaNirbhar Nidhi)
ministry: Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs

interest_subvention.note: 7% interest subsidy on timely repayment, credited quarterly.

digital_cashback.note: Cashback up to ₹100 per month on executing eligible digital transactions.

effective_interest_rate_note: Effective rate is roughly 2% after the 7% subvention on timely repayment.
eligibility_human: Urban street vendors (hawkers, thela walas) specifically. Available in cycles of ₹10,000, ₹20,000, and ₹50,000 upon successful repayment of the previous cycle.

documents_required.name: Certificate of Vending (CoV) / Identity Card issued by ULB

pros: Collateral-free fast-track loan.
Increases credit limit in cycles (10k -> 20k -> 50k).
cons: Strictly limited to recognized urban street vendors.
Short repayment tenure (12 months per cycle).
application_steps: Procure a Letter of Recommendation (LoR) or Certificate of Vending from the Urban Local Body.
Apply online via the SVAVANidhi portal or mobile app.
Amount is disbursed directly to the bank account.

name: Mukhyamantri Yuva Udyami Vikas Abhiyan (MYUVA)
ministry: Department of MSME, Govt of Uttar Pradesh
effective_interest_rate_note: 100% interest subsidy for 4 years on loans up to ₹5 lakh (Phase 1). 50% interest subsidy for 3 years on expansion loans from ₹10 lakh to ₹20 lakh (Phase 2).
eligibility_human: Permanent residents of UP aged 21-40 with a minimum 8th-grade education setting up a new business. Priority is given to those who have completed government training programs.
pros: Complete 100% interest subsidy for the first 4 years.
Direct pathway to scale up funding (₹10L - ₹20L) in Phase 2.
cons: No upfront capital grant/margin money subsidy, only interest subvention.
application_steps: Register on the Directorate of Industries UPMSME portal.
Select the scheme from the beneficiary section and fill out details.

name: Mukhyamantri Yuva Udyami Yojana
ministry: Department of Industries, Govt of Bihar

women_transgender.note: A parallel scheme (Mukhyamantri Mahila Udyami Yojana) exists for women and transgender applicants.

effective_interest_rate_note: 50% of the assistance (up to ₹5L) is a non-repayable grant. The remaining 50% is a nominal 1% interest loan (or 0% for specific categories).
eligibility_human: Male applicants from General and Backward Classes aged 18-50 who are permanent residents of Bihar with at least a 10+2/ITI/Diploma education.
pros: Massive 50% non-repayable grant on project cost.
Mandatory skill training provided to ensure business viability.
cons: Highly competitive; beneficiaries are often selected via computerized randomization (lottery).
Application windows open only for specific short durations.
application_steps: Register on Udyami Bihar portal using Aadhaar.
Fill online application and upload certificates.
Await selection list (often randomized draft list).

name: Mukhyamantri Udyam Kranti Yojana
ministry: Department of MSME, Govt of MP
effective_interest_rate_note: Borrower receives a 3% interest subsidy per annum and full CGTMSE guarantee fee waiver.
eligibility_human: Youth aged 18 to 45 who are 10th pass and permanent residents of MP. They must not have taken loans under other self-employment schemes.
pros: Collateral-free loans up to ₹50 lakh for manufacturing and ₹25 lakh for services/trading.
Government covers the CGTMSE guarantee fee, reducing borrowing costs.
cons: Family income limit restrictions apply.
application_steps: Apply online via MP Online Samast portal.
Application is forwarded to banks for loan sanctioning.

name: Stand-Up India Scheme
ministry: Ministry of Finance
effective_interest_rate_note: Lowest applicable rate of the bank for that rating category (MCLR + 3% + tenor premium).
eligibility_human: At least 18 years old. Must be SC, ST, or a Woman entrepreneur. Must be setting up a greenfield (new) enterprise. In case of non-individual enterprises, 51% of the shareholding must be held by SC/ST or Women.
pros: Facilitates massive bank loans between ₹10 lakh and ₹1 Crore.
Covers up to 85% of the project cost.
cons: No direct subsidy/grant component.
Strictly greenfield (new) projects only.
application_steps: Register on Stand-Up Mitra portal.
Fill out the application to connect with a Lead District Manager (LDM) or preferred bank branch.
Submit DPR and await bank processing.

name: Credit Linked Capital Subsidy Scheme (CLCSS)
ministry: Ministry of MSME

sc_st_women_ner_hill_aspirational.note: Relaxed eligibility for any technology upgradation

effective_interest_rate_note: Market rate; subsidy reduces effective principal.
eligibility_human: Micro & Small Enterprises with Udyam Registration in manufacturing/services upgrading their technology.
pros: Direct 15% capital subsidy reduces project cost.
cons: Requires bank sanction first — two-step process.
application_steps: Approach bank branch for in-principle sanction.
Bank applies for subsidy via online MIS portal.

name: Start-up Village Entrepreneurship Programme (SVEP)
ministry: Ministry of Rural Development
effective_interest_rate_note: CEF (Community Enterprise Fund) loans provided at 1% per month (12% annually) via the Block Level Federation (BLF).
eligibility_human: Rural entrepreneurs who are members of Self Help Groups (SHGs) or their family members under the DAY-NRLM umbrella.
pros: Access to highly localized credit without collateral.
Handholding support from Community Resource Persons for Enterprise Promotion (CRP-EP) for business planning.
cons: Only available in approved SVEP blocks.
Small ticket size limits scaling.
application_steps: Contact local CRP-EP or Village Organization.
CRP-EP assists in drafting a business plan.
Plan is approved by Block Level Federation (BLF) which disperses the CEF loan.

name: PM Formalisation of Micro Food Processing Enterprises (PMFME)
ministry: Ministry of Food Processing Industries

shg_seed_capital.note: Seed capital of ₹40,000 per SHG member for working capital and small tools.

effective_interest_rate_note: Standard term loan interest rates apply. Interest subvention available if combined with Agri Infrastructure Fund (AIF).
eligibility_human: Individual micro food processing entrepreneurs, Farmer Producer Organizations (FPOs), SHGs, and Cooperatives focusing on 'One District One Product' (ODOP) or other food processing activities.
pros: Provides 35% credit-linked capital subsidy up to ₹10 lakh.
Seed capital of ₹40,000 provided to SHG members for working capital.
cons: Strictly limited to the food processing sector.
application_steps: Register on the PMFME portal.
Submit application and system-generated DPR.
District Level Committee recommends the application to banks.

name: Credit Guarantee Fund Trust for Micro and Small Enterprises (CGTMSE)
ministry: Ministry of MSME

women_sc_st_ner.note: Guarantee cover is up to 85% for Micro enterprises up to ₹5 lakh, Women, SC/ST, and units in NER. Standard cover is 75%.

effective_interest_rate_note: Reduces lending risk, ensuring collateral-free loans. A minor Annual Guarantee Fee (AGF) is charged (often absorbed by state schemes).
eligibility_human: Any new or existing Micro and Small Enterprise (MSE) requiring collateral-free credit facilities up to ₹10 Crore (recent enhancement) from eligible banks.
pros: Removes the primary bottleneck for MSEs: the lack of collateral/third-party guarantee.
Cover limit significantly expanded to ₹10 Crore.
cons: It is not a standalone loan; it applies as a backend guarantee to loans sanctioned under other terms.
application_steps: Approach an MLI (bank) for a business loan.
Request the bank to cover the loan under the CGTMSE scheme.
The bank applies for the guarantee cover online.

name: Chief Minister Employment Generation Programme (CMEGP) Maharashtra
ministry: Directorate of Industries, Maharashtra
implementing_agency: DIC and Maharashtra Khadi & Village Industries Board

sc_st_women_minorities_rural.note: General category gets 15% (urban) / 25% (rural). Special categories get 25% (urban) / 35% (rural).

effective_interest_rate_note: Standard bank rates apply. Upfront margin money subsidy reduces the principal loan burden.
eligibility_human: Maharashtra residents aged 18-45 setting up a new unit. Age relaxed up to 50 for special categories. Education must be 7th pass for projects above ₹10L and 10th pass for projects above ₹25L.
pros: Massive 15–35% direct subsidy on project cost.
Upper limit of ₹50 Lakh for manufacturing and ₹20 Lakh for services.
cons: Not available for business expansion (strictly greenfield).
If you have already availed PMEGP or PMRY, you are disqualified.
application_steps: Submit application on maha-cmegp.gov.in.
DIC screens the application and forwards it to your selected bank.
Bank disburses loan; government margin money is held in a 3-year term deposit before being adjusted against the loan.

name: Annasaheb Patil Mahamandal Karj Yojana
ministry: Annasaheb Patil Arthik Vikas Mahamandal
effective_interest_rate_note: 100% interest subvention (Vyaj Partava). Borrower pays bank EMIs, and the government refunds the exact interest amount to their Aadhaar-linked bank account.
eligibility_human: Maharashtra residents aged 18 to 60 belonging to the Maratha community (Economically Backward Class). Applicant must NOT be an income-tax payer.
pros: Effectively zero interest cost for loans up to ₹50 Lakh.
Applicable for both new setups and expansions of existing businesses.
cons: Missed EMIs immediately cancel the interest refund (strict timely repayment clause).
Restricted exclusively to non-tax paying members of the Maratha/EBC community.
application_steps: Register on udyog.mahaswayam.gov.in and generate an LOI (Letter of Intent).
Take the LOI to an empanelled bank and secure loan sanction.
Submit bank sanction details back to the Mahamandal to start the monthly/quarterly Vyaj Partava (interest refund) cycle.

name: One District One Product (ODOP) Margin Money Scheme
ministry: Department of MSME, Govt of UP

large_projects.note: Projects over ₹50L get 10% margin money or max ₹20L, whichever is higher.

effective_interest_rate_note: Standard bank lending rates apply.
eligibility_human: UP residents above 18 setting up a new unit strictly aligned with their district's identified ODOP product (e.g., Leather in Kanpur, Brass in Moradabad).

documents_required.name: Detailed Project Report tailored to ODOP item

pros: 25% capital subsidy for projects up to ₹25 lakh.
Highly integrated with local supply chains and district branding.
cons: Restricted strictly to the specific product mapped to the applicant's home district.
application_steps: Verify your district's designated ODOP product on the official portal.
Submit online application to District Industries Centre (DIC).
Task Force Committee routes it to the bank for collateral-free (CGTMSE) or standard loan sanction.

name: Mukhyamantri Mahila Udyami Yojana
ministry: Department of Industries, Govt of Bihar
effective_interest_rate_note: 50% is a direct non-repayable grant. The remaining 50% is a 100% interest-free loan to be repaid in 84 installments.
eligibility_human: Women and Transgender residents of Bihar aged 18-50 from ANY caste category, possessing at least 10+2/ITI/Diploma education.

documents_required.name: Current Bank Account Details (opened in the name of the firm)

pros: 0% interest on the loan component.
Open to all women regardless of caste (General, SC, ST, OBC).
cons: Strict application windows (the portal opens for limited days a year).
Beneficiaries are often drawn via a lottery system due to oversubscription.
application_steps: Register an MSME Udyam profile or form a proprietorship firm.
Open a current bank account in the firm's name.
Apply online on the Udyami portal during the active window.

name: MSME Sustainable (ZED) Certification Scheme
ministry: Ministry of MSME

women_sc_st_ner.note: Women, SC/ST, and NER MSMEs receive a 100% subsidy on certification costs. Micro gets 80%, Small 60%, Medium 50% generally.

effective_interest_rate_note: Not a loan scheme. Several state banks (like SBI) offer a 0.5% concession on interest rates for ZED-certified MSMEs.
eligibility_human: All Udyam registered manufacturing MSMEs aiming to improve processes to 'Zero Defect, Zero Effect' environmental standards.

documents_required.name: Undertaking for basic parameters (for Bronze level)

pros: Massive concessions (up to ₹3 Lakh) on purchasing plant/machinery to achieve zero defect.
ZED certified units receive priority in government e-Marketplace (GeM) procurement.
cons: Not a direct capital financing scheme for setting up a business.
Strict compliance audits required for Silver and Gold tiers.
application_steps: Take the ZED pledge online using your Udyam number (Free).
Apply for Bronze certification via desktop assessment.
Apply for financial assistance for testing/machinery upgrades after certification.

name: Startup India Seed Fund Scheme (SISFS)
ministry: Ministry of Commerce and Industry (DPIIT)
effective_interest_rate_note: Up to ₹20 Lakhs provided as an outright grant for PoC/prototype. Up to ₹50 Lakhs provided as convertible debentures/debt for market entry.
eligibility_human: DPIIT-recognized startups incorporated less than 2 years ago at the time of application, solving a problem through technology/innovation.
pros: Provides vital bridge capital without giving away immediate equity (via convertible notes/grants).
Ties startups directly to high-quality incubator mentorship.
cons: Cannot be utilized if the startup has already raised more than ₹10 Lakhs from angel/VC sources.
The incubator evaluates the pitch, meaning rejection rates can be high.
application_steps: Startup applies on the portal and selects up to 3 preferred incubators.
Incubators evaluate applications in sequence (28-day window).
Shortlisted startups pitch to the Incubator Seed Management Committee (ISMC).

name: Agriculture Infrastructure Fund (AIF)
ministry: Ministry of Agriculture & Farmers Welfare
effective_interest_rate_note: A massive 3% per annum interest subvention is provided on loans up to ₹2 Crore for a maximum period of 7 years. CGTMSE fee is also paid by the Govt for loans up to ₹2 Crore.
eligibility_human: Farmers, FPOs, PACS, Marketing Cooperative Societies, SHGs, and Agri-entrepreneurs/Startups building post-harvest infrastructure (cold storage, warehouses, assaying units, etc.).

documents_required.name: Record of Rights (Land Documents) or Lease Agreement

pros: Interest rate capped by the government; effectively making agri-infra loans incredibly cheap.
Can be converged with other capital subsidy schemes (like PMFME or state agri schemes) for dual benefits.
cons: Strictly for infrastructure/assets, not for crop production or standard working capital.
application_steps: Beneficiary registers on the AIF portal and uploads the DPR.
The application is routed to the selected lending institution.
Bank sanctions the loan and claims the 3% interest subvention automatically via the portal.

name: Pradhan Mantri Matsya Sampada Yojana (PMMSY)
ministry: Ministry of Fisheries, Animal Husbandry and Dairying
implementing_agency: National Fisheries Development Board (NFDB) / State Fisheries Dept

sc_st_women.note: Subsidy jumps to 60% of the unit cost for Women and SC/ST categories.

effective_interest_rate_note: Direct capital grant calculated against the normative unit cost of the project.
eligibility_human: Fishers, Fish farmers, Fish vendors, SHGs, and private entrepreneurs looking to build fisheries infrastructure (ponds, hatcheries, cold chains, biofloc, ice plants).

documents_required.name: Land Lease (min 7-10 years) or Ownership Docs

pros: Incredible 40-60% backend subsidy on a massive list of approved activities (from buying a two-wheeler with an ice box to building a ₹2 Cr cold storage).
cons: Often requires the beneficiary to spend their own money/take a loan first before the backend subsidy is released.
application_steps: Prepare a proposal based on PMMSY unit costs.
Submit application to the District Fisheries Officer (DFO).
State Level Approval Committee clears the project and releases funds in tranches based on construction progress.

name: Mukhyamantri Laghu Udyog Protsahan Yojana (MLUPY)
ministry: Department of Industries, Govt of Rajasthan

slab_based.note: 8% subsidy on loans up to ₹25 Lakh; 6% on loans ₹25L to ₹5 Cr; 5% on loans ₹5 Cr to ₹10 Cr.

effective_interest_rate_note: Massively reduces bank interest rates via state subvention. A typical 10% loan becomes a 2% loan for a micro-entrepreneur borrowing ₹25 Lakh.
eligibility_human: Individuals above 18 years, SHGs, and MSMEs establishing new enterprises or expanding existing ones in Rajasthan.
pros: Covers trading businesses (which are often excluded from central MSME schemes).
Can be used for expanding existing units, not just new ones.
cons: No upfront capital subsidy; relies on the entrepreneur successfully securing a bank loan first.
application_steps: Log in via Rajasthan SSO Portal.
Apply under MLUPY and submit to DIC online.
DIC forwards to the bank. Once the loan is sanctioned, interest subsidy is credited quarterly.

name: Mukhyamantri Krushi Udyog Yojana (MKUY)
ministry: Agriculture & Farmers' Empowerment Department

sc_st_women_agri_graduates.note: Women, SC/ST, Transgender, and Agri-graduates receive an enhanced 50% capital subsidy up to ₹1 Crore.

effective_interest_rate_note: Direct capital subsidy.
eligibility_human: Residents of Odisha above 18 setting up commercial agri-enterprises. Must have 8th standard pass for projects over ₹10 Lakh. Transgender entrepreneurs are fully eligible.

documents_required.name: Valid Record of Rights (RoR) / 15-year Lease Deed

pros: Extremely high upper cap (₹1 Crore subsidy limit per family).
Explicitly inclusive of Transgender entrepreneurs and Women with 50% subsidy rates.
cons: Stringent land requirements (15-year lease deed required if rented).
Application fee of ₹2000 is required.
application_steps: Register on the MKUY portal with Aadhaar.
Upload DPR and land records.
Receive Go-Ahead Letter from APICOL after field verification.
Complete the project within 2 years to claim the subsidy.

name: National Livestock Mission (NLM) - Entrepreneurship Development Programme
ministry: Ministry of Fisheries, Animal Husbandry & Dairying

tribal_fra.note: 90% PM-JUGA Subsidy specifically for Tribal (FRA) Beneficiaries in designated areas.

effective_interest_rate_note: A massive direct capital subsidy reduces the principal. Standard bank loan interest rates apply to the remaining 50% financed by the applicant.
eligibility_human: Individuals, SHGs, FPOs, JLGs, and Section 8 companies undertaking livestock breeding. Must have their own or leased land and secure a bank loan sanction/guarantee first.
pros: 50% capital subsidy with massive ceilings: ₹50L for Sheep/Goat (500+25 unit), ₹25L for Poultry (1000 layers), ₹30L for Piggery, and ₹50L for Fodder units.
Now explicitly covers Horse, Donkey, and Camel entrepreneurship up to ₹50 Lakh.
cons: Subsidy is strictly back-ended and released in two tranches via SIDBI only after the bank releases its first installment and project milestones are verified.
application_steps: Submit DPR and KYC online on the UdyamiMitra NLM portal.
The State Implementing Agency (SIA) scrutinizes and recommends the project to a bank.
Bank sanctions the loan. SIDBI releases 50% of the subsidy amount to the bank.
Second half of subsidy released after project completion and SIA verification.

name: Agri-Clinics and Agri-Business Centres Scheme (ACABC)
ministry: Ministry of Agriculture and Farmers' Welfare

sc_st_women_ner_hill.note: 44% composite subsidy for Women, SC/ST, and all candidates from North-Eastern and Hill states.

group_projects.note: Ceiling expands to ₹100 lakhs for a group project comprising at least 5 trained persons.

effective_interest_rate_note: No interest is charged on the subsidy portion of the loan, as the subsidy is released upfront and kept in a lock-in period of 3 years.
eligibility_human: Graduates/Diploma holders in Agriculture/Allied subjects, or Intermediate (10+2) with 55% marks in agriculture. Must undergo mandatory 2-month training at Nodal Training Institutes under MANAGE.
pros: Creates direct self-employment for educated youth by funding ventures like crop advisory clinics, soil testing labs, and veterinary services.
No margin money required for loans up to ₹5 Lakhs.
cons: Strict educational requirements exclude the general farming public.
application_steps: Apply for and complete the free residential training program via an approved Nodal Training Institute (NTI).
Prepare a DPR during the training.
Submit the DPR and NTI certificate to a bank for term loan sanction.

name: Pradhan Mantri Mudra Yojana (PMMY) – Tarun / Tarun Plus
ministry: Ministry of Finance
effective_interest_rate_note: Ranges from 9% to 12% depending on the lender; strictly collateral-free under CGTMSE/CGFMU.
eligibility_human: Established micro-businesses requiring capital for expansion. To qualify for 'Tarun Plus' (up to ₹20L), the applicant must have successfully repaid a previous Mudra loan.
pros: Recently enhanced loan limit up to ₹20 Lakh (Tarun Plus) provides serious scale-up capital.
Can be availed as a mix of Term Loan (for machinery) and Cash Credit/Overdraft (working capital).
cons: No direct subsidy component.
Requires solid financial track record (ITRs, GST returns) unlike the Shishu tier.
application_steps: Prepare detailed financials (ITR, GST, Projected sales).
Apply via Udyamimitra portal or directly at a bank branch where the current account is maintained.
Bank conducts field inspection and credit appraisal before sanctioning.

name: Mission Shakti Loan Scheme (Odisha)
ministry: Mission Shakti Department, Govt of Odisha
effective_interest_rate_note: 100% Interest Subvention. State government refunds the entire interest amount to the SHG's account for loans up to ₹10 Lakhs, resulting in a 0% effective interest rate.
eligibility_human: Women Self Help Groups (WSHGs) in Odisha who borrow from institutional banks and repay their installments regularly.
pros: Provides entirely interest-free working and term capital up to ₹10 Lakhs for women collectives.
Can be converged with other schemes like Mukta Yojana for community contracting.
cons: Strictly linked to prompt repayment. A single default/delay disqualifies the SHG from the interest refund for that cycle.
application_steps: WSHG prepares a micro-credit plan and applies for a loan at their linked bank branch.
Bank disburses the loan.
Upon timely payment of EMIs, the interest portion is automatically subvented to the SHG account.

name: Mukhyamantri Gramodyog Rojgar Yojana (MMGRY)
ministry: MSME & Export Promotion, Govt of UP

reserved_categories.note: SC, ST, OBC, Minorities, Women, and PwD get 100% interest subvention (0% loan). General category men get interest subvention leaving them to pay a fixed 4%.

effective_interest_rate_note: 0% for women/reserved categories; 4% for general category. The state covers the difference against standard bank lending rates.
eligibility_human: Unemployed rural youth and traditional artisans of UP aged 18-50. Priority given to ITI pass outs and those trained under KVIB/Government programs.
pros: Excellent mechanism for rural micro-entrepreneurs to secure up to ₹10 Lakh entirely interest-free (for reserved categories/women).
Requires no collateral as it leverages CGTMSE.
cons: Strictly limited to rural populations (gram panchayat areas).
application_steps: Register and fill out the online application on the UPKVIB portal.
The District Task Force Committee interviews the candidate and selects beneficiaries.
Bank disburses the loan; KVIB pays the interest subvention amount directly to the bank.

name: MSME Innovative Scheme (Incubation Component)
ministry: Ministry of MSME
effective_interest_rate_note: Non-repayable direct grant for prototype development.
eligibility_human: Udyam-registered MSMEs or individual innovators (students/entrepreneurs) who are incubated at a recognized Host Institution (HI) like an IIT, NIT, or established tech incubator.

documents_required.name: Letter of Support from Host Institution

pros: Provides up to ₹15 Lakhs as an absolute grant (free money) with zero equity taken by the government.
Binds the innovator directly with top-tier technical mentoring at Host Institutions.
cons: Highly competitive; the idea must display clear commercialization potential and technological merit.
application_steps: Innovator connects with an approved Host Institution.
Submit the idea on the MSME Innovative portal.
The idea is vetted by local and national committees. If approved, funds are released to the HI to support the prototype build.

name: Pradhan Mantri Mudra Yojana (PMMY) – Kishor
ministry: Ministry of Finance
implementing_agency: MUDRA Ltd / Commercial Banks / RRBs / NBFCs
effective_interest_rate_note: Bank-determined rates (typically 8.5% to 11.5%). 100% collateral-free backed by the Credit Guarantee Fund for Micro Units (CGFMU).
eligibility_human: Existing micro-enterprises or promising new businesses that have outgrown the Shishu tier (₹50k) and require working capital or machinery purchases up to ₹5 Lakh.

documents_required.name: Quotations for Machinery / Raw Materials to be bought

pros: No collateral or third-party guarantee required.
Can be sanctioned as a composite loan (term loan for asset purchase + Mudra Card overdraft for daily operations).
cons: Zero capital subsidy or interest waiver.
Requires established proof of business operations or firm purchase quotations.
application_steps: Gather asset quotations and 6-month bank statement.
Apply through the UdyamiMitra online portal or approach the branch where current/savings account is held.
Bank completes technical appraisal and sanctions loan under CGFMU guarantee.

name: Sub-Mission on Agricultural Mechanization (SMAM)
ministry: Ministry of Agriculture & Farmers Welfare
implementing_agency: State Departments of Agriculture / Mechanization Divisions

sc_st_women_small_farmers.note: Individual equipment subsidy is 50% for SC, ST, Small/Marginal Farmers, and Women (40% for General). Custom Hiring Centre (CHC) projects get up to 40% subsidy up to ₹24 Lakh on a ₹60 Lakh project.

effective_interest_rate_note: Direct capital subsidy credited via DBT to purchase farm equipment or establish Custom Hiring Centres (CHCs).
eligibility_human: Individual farmers, rural entrepreneurs, FPOs, Cooperatives, and SHGs. To set up a Custom Hiring Centre (CHC), the entrepreneur must establish equipment availability for local smallholders.

documents_required.name: Valid Quotation from Empanelled Farm Machinery Dealer

pros: Substantial 40% to 50% capital subsidy on expensive equipment (tractors, harvesters, laser levelers, drone sprayers).
Creates sustainable rental income models through Custom Hiring Centres.
cons: Subsidies are quota-driven and tied to annual state budget releases.
Purchases must be made strictly from government-empanelled manufacturers/dealers.
application_steps: Register on the agrimachinery.nic.in DBT portal.
Select desired farm machinery / CHC model and upload dealer quotation and land documents.
Receive online approval permit, purchase equipment, and submit serial/chassis number for physical verification.
Subsidy is credited directly to the linked bank account.

name: Pradhan Mantri Van Dhan Yojana (PMVDY)
ministry: Ministry of Tribal Affairs
implementing_agency: TRIFED / State Forest & Tribal Development Agencies
effective_interest_rate_note: 100% grant assistance from the Central Government to establish a Van Dhan Vikas Kendra (VDVK). Not a loan.
eligibility_human: Tribal forest gatherers and forest dwellers organized into SHGs (15 SHGs with roughly 20 members each form 1 Van Dhan Vikas Kendra of 300 gatherers). At least 60% of members must be Scheduled Tribes.

documents_required.name: Van Dhan SHG Resolution & Bank Account

pros: 100% non-repayable central grant of ₹15 Lakh per Kendra for value addition, primary processing, toolkits, and packaging.
Eliminates exploitative middlemen by facilitating value addition for Minor Forest Produce (MFP) locally.
cons: Strictly for collective tribal groups; individual entrepreneurs cannot apply on their own.
application_steps: Form 15 SHGs under Gram Sabha guidance and federate into a Van Dhan Vikas Kendra.
Submit Kendra proposal to District Collector / District Forest Officer (DFO).
State Nodal Agency submits proposal to TRIFED for sanction and release of funds.

name: Special Credit Linked Capital Subsidy Scheme (SCLCSS for SC-ST)
ministry: Ministry of Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises
effective_interest_rate_note: Direct upfront capital subsidy reducing the net loan principal.
eligibility_human: SC/ST entrepreneurs who own at least 51% shareholding in an Udyam-registered Micro or Small Enterprise purchasing modern plant, machinery, or service equipment via institutional loan.
pros: 25% capital subsidy (higher than standard CLCSS's 15%) up to a maximum of ₹25 Lakh.
Covers both manufacturing equipment and service sector machinery/tools.
cons: Second-hand or used machinery is strictly ineligible.
Requires commercial bank term loan sanction prior to subsidy release.
application_steps: Secure an institutional term loan from a commercial bank for eligible new machinery.
Bank submits the SCLCSS claim via the online MIS portal to SIDBI/DCMSME.
Upon verification, subsidy is disbursed to the bank and kept in a 3-year term deposit receipt (TDR) before final adjustment.

name: MSME Competitive (LEAN) Scheme
ministry: Ministry of Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises

women_sc_st_ner.note: 95% government contribution for MSMEs owned by SC/ST/Women entrepreneurs or located in NER.

effective_interest_rate_note: Government provides up to 90% reimbursement of the LEAN consultant implementation fee.
eligibility_human: Any manufacturing MSME with a valid Udyam Registration looking to eliminate waste, improve quality, reduce inventory, and adopt 5S/Kaizen/Poka-Yoke techniques.
pros: 90% of the consultant implementation fees are borne by the Central Government.
Substantially improves workshop floor efficiency and cuts manufacturing cycle times.
cons: Not for purchasing capital machinery or raw materials.
Requires internal operational discipline and time investment from staff.
application_steps: Take the free online LEAN Pledge on lean.msme.gov.in.
Apply for Basic, Intermediate, or Advanced level implementation.
Empanelled QCI/NPC LEAN consultants are assigned to the factory floor to execute Kaizen/5S projects.

name: Credit Guarantee Scheme for Startups (CGSS)
ministry: Ministry of Commerce and Industry (DPIIT)
effective_interest_rate_note: Guarantees collateral-free bank loans and venture debt up to ₹10 Crore per startup. Guarantee cover is up to 80% for loans up to ₹3 Crore and up to 75% for loans between ₹3 Crore and ₹10 Crore.
eligibility_human: DPIIT-recognized startups that have reached the commercial stage with proven business traction, requiring collateral-free venture debt or term credit from Member Lending Institutions (MLIs) or AIFs.

documents_required.name: Debt Pitch Deck & Cash Flow Projections

pros: Enables high-growth startups to raise non-dilutive debt up to ₹10 Crore without physical collateral.
Covers both conventional bank loans and venture debt funds.
cons: Startups must be generating stable commercial revenue (not suitable for raw ideation stage).
Lenders charge an Annual Guarantee Fee (AGF) of 1.5% to 2%.
application_steps: Obtain DPIIT Recognition on startupindia.gov.in.
Approach an empanelled Member Lending Institution (MLI) or participating Venture Debt fund.
Lender conducts due diligence and registers the loan under NCGTC for credit guarantee cover.

name: Scheme of Fund for Regeneration of Traditional Industries (SFURTI)
ministry: Ministry of MSME

ner_and_jk.note: For North Eastern Region and J&K, the government covers up to 95% of the Hard Intervention cost.

effective_interest_rate_note: Direct central grant for establishing common facility centres (CFCs), not a bank loan. Maximum assistance is ₹2.5 Crore for Regular Clusters (up to 500 artisans) and ₹8 Crore for Major Clusters (>500 artisans).
eligibility_human: Artisan guilds, cooperatives, consortiums, networks of enterprises, and SHGs engaged in traditional industries (Khadi, Coir, Bamboo, Honey, Handicrafts) looking to form a production cluster. Minimum concentration required is usually 500 beneficiary families.

documents_required.name: Detailed Project Report (DPR) prepared by Technical Agency

pros: Massive non-repayable grant up to ₹8 Crore for building heavy infrastructure (Common Facility Centres) for rural artisans.
Pays for 'Soft Interventions' (skill training, design development) entirely at 100% government cost.
cons: Cannot be accessed by a single individual; requires organizing hundreds of rural artisans into a formal Special Purpose Vehicle (SPV).
application_steps: Identify a dense pocket of traditional artisans and form an SPV/Cooperative.
Engage an empanelled Technical Agency (TA) to draft a diagnostic study and DPR.
Submit DPR to a Nodal Agency (like KVIC).
Scheme Steering Committee (SSC) at the Ministry level approves the grant and releases funds in tranches.

name: RKVY-RAFTAAR Agripreneurship Seed Grant
ministry: Ministry of Agriculture & Farmers' Welfare

idea_stage.note: Idea/Pre-Seed stage innovators can get a 100% grant of ₹5 Lakh as a monthly stipend/prototype fund before reaching the Seed stage.

effective_interest_rate_note: 100% Grant-in-aid; no repayment required.
eligibility_human: Registered DPIIT startups, Private Limited Companies, or LLPs with a Minimum Viable Product (MVP) operating in agriculture, horticulture, or allied rural sectors. Must undergo residency at an R-ABI.
nodal_agencies: Host R-ABIs (e.g., IIT BHU, MANAGE, TNAU)
pros: Up to ₹25 Lakh pure seed grant to launch an agri-product commercially.
Direct linkage with elite Agribusiness Incubators (R-ABIs) for technical mentoring and lab access.
cons: The startup must contribute 15% of the project cost from their own funds to unlock the ₹25 Lakh grant.
Cannot be drawing parallel funding from another government ministry for the same prototype.
application_steps: Apply during an open cohort call at an approved RKVY-RAFTAAR Agribusiness Incubator (R-ABI).
Pitch before the RKVY-RAFTAAR Incubation Committee (RIC).
Complete the mandatory incubation residency (virtual/physical).
Grant is released in milestone-based installments.

name: Animal Husbandry Infrastructure Development Fund (AHIDF)
ministry: Department of Animal Husbandry and Dairying (DAHD)

credit_guarantee.note: A 25% credit guarantee cover is provided for MSMEs from the ₹750 Cr Credit Guarantee Fund.

effective_interest_rate_note: DAHD provides a 3% per annum interest subvention on the term loan for a period of up to 8 years (including 2 years moratorium).
eligibility_human: FPOs, MSMEs, Section 8 Companies, and Private Entrepreneurs establishing dairy processing, meat processing, animal feed plants, or breed multiplication farms.

documents_required.name: MSME Udyam Registration (if claiming MSME guarantee)

pros: Massively reduces the interest burden for large-scale rural processing plants.
No upper limit on the loan amount eligible for the 3% subvention (though DAHD appraises projects >₹50 Cr at the secretary level).
cons: Borrower must contribute at least 10% (MSME) or 25% (Non-MSME) as margin money.
Strictly for post-production processing and infra, not for simply buying cattle.
application_steps: Upload DPR and apply on the UdyamiMitra AHIDF portal selecting preferred lender.
DAHD conducts an initial 'LAF screening'.
Application moves to the bank branch; bank sanctions loan within 30 days.
DAHD Project Approval Committee signs off, and interest subvention is remitted directly to the bank account annually.

name: ASPIRE Seed Fund for Incubatees
ministry: Ministry of MSME
effective_interest_rate_note: Direct seed grant transferred in milestone-based tranches; no repayment required.
eligibility_human: Individual innovators, pre-revenue, or early-revenue rural/agri-tech startups enrolled as incubatees at an ASPIRE-approved Technology Business Incubator (TBI).
pros: Disburses ₹5 Lakh to ₹50 Lakh to individuals for validating prototypes and launching rural-focused technologies.
Comes with physical workspace, machinery access, and market linkage from the TBI.
cons: Funding is tightly tied to achieving milestones; failure to progress may halt subsequent tranches.
application_steps: Locate an active ASPIRE TBI using the state-wise filter on aspire.msme.gov.in.
Apply directly to the incubator with a short concept note.
Pitch the idea; upon selection, sign an incubatee agreement.
Demonstrate pilot progress to unlock seed funds from the TBI's ₹1 Crore corpus.

name: DAY-NRLM Community Investment Fund (CIF)
ministry: Ministry of Rural Development
effective_interest_rate_note: A highly subsidized rotating fund. Interest rates vary slightly by state but are usually between 6% and 9% per annum, decided by the Cluster Level Federation (CLF).
eligibility_human: Rural women SHGs that have completed at least 6 months of active existence, practiced 'Panchasutra' (regular meetings, savings, internal lending), and received a Revolving Fund (RF).
pros: Allows SHGs to access up to ₹2.5 Lakh for internal lending without approaching a formal bank.
Forms the foundation capital for rural women to scale up into 'Lakhpati Didis' (annual income > ₹1 Lakh).
cons: Money is technically a loan to the SHG from the CLF in perpetuity; it must be repaid into the community pool.
application_steps: SHG drafts a Micro-Investment Plan (MIP) identifying the livelihood needs of its members.
MIP is appraised by the Village Organization (VO).
Cluster Level Federation (CLF) releases the CIF amount to the VO, which transfers it to the SHG's bank account.

name: National Beekeeping & Honey Mission (NBHM)
ministry: Ministry of Agriculture & Farmers Welfare

women_and_shgs.note: 100% subsidy for women groups and state departmental projects up to specified limits.

effective_interest_rate_note: Direct capital grant for purchasing bee colonies, hives, and establishing Honey extraction/processing units.
eligibility_human: Individual beekeepers, FPOs, FPCs, SHGs, and Cooperatives seeking to expand beekeeping or establish Custom Hiring Centres (CHCs) for honey extraction.
pros: Subsidizes up to 75% of the cost for FPOs to set up ₹1 Crore Honey Processing & Extraction Custom Hiring Centres.
Provides direct financial aid for purchasing bee boxes and colonies for individual farmers.
cons: Beneficiary must be formally registered on the Madhukranti traceability portal.
application_steps: Register on the Madhukranti portal to generate a Beekeeper ID.
Submit application to the State Horticulture Department or NBB.
Funds are released via DBT directly or routed to the empanelled equipment manufacturer.

name: Yuva Sahakar - Cooperative Enterprise Support and Innovation Scheme
ministry: Ministry of Cooperation

special_categories.note: 2% interest subvention for cooperatives that are 100% owned by Women, SC, ST, or PwD. NCDC finances up to 80% of the project cost for these categories (70% for General).

effective_interest_rate_note: Long-term term loan up to 5 years. A 2% interest subvention is provided on the applicable NCDC rate for special category cooperatives.
eligibility_human: Cooperative societies and FPOs registered under any State/Central Act that have been in operation for at least 3 months. Ideally suited for youth-driven agritech, food processing, or rural service cooperatives.
pros: Provides massive capital (up to ₹3 Crore) for rural youth cooperatives to scale modern businesses.
Lower margin money requirements for women and SC/ST groups.
cons: Must be a formally registered cooperative society; individual farmers or unregistered SHGs cannot apply.
application_steps: Cooperative board passes a resolution for expansion.
Submit DPR to the State Govt or directly to the NCDC Regional Directorate.
NCDC evaluates technical viability and sanctions the term loan directly or via the State.

name: Concessional Credit / Weaver MUDRA Scheme
ministry: Ministry of Textiles

handloom_organizations.note: For Handloom Organizations, margin money is 20% subject to a maximum of ₹20 Lakh (calculated at ₹2 Lakh per 100 weavers).

effective_interest_rate_note: Loans are provided at a concessional interest rate of 6% for a period of 3 years. The Government of India bears the remaining interest burden (subvention capped at 7%).
eligibility_human: Individual handloom weavers, weaver entrepreneurs, and Handloom Organizations (Master Weavers, SHGs, Consortia) requiring working capital for yarn, dyes, or loom upgrades.
pros: Extremely affordable 6% flat interest rate for weavers.
Upfront 20% margin money subsidy directly reduces the borrower's out-of-pocket contribution.
Credit guarantee fees are fully paid by the Government for 3 years.
cons: Margin money is capped at a strict ₹25,000 for individual weavers, meaning it primarily covers micro-loans.
application_steps: Obtain a Pehchan Card (Weaver ID).
Apply through the local Weavers Service Centre (WSC) or directly at a participating bank.
Bank sanctions the working capital limit (often via a RuPay Mudra Card) and claims subvention via the PNB portal.

name: Bhoomihina Agriculturist Loan & Resources Augmentation Model (BALARAM)
ministry: Agriculture & Farmers' Empowerment Department

interest_free_tier.note: Loans up to ₹5,000 are entirely interest-free. Standard agricultural subvention rates apply above that.

effective_interest_rate_note: Uses social collateral. State crop loan rules govern the interest rate, with deep subventions for prompt repayment.
eligibility_human: Strictly for tenant farmers, sharecroppers, and landless agricultural laborers in Odisha. Applicants must form a Joint Liability Group (JLG) of 5 to 10 members.

documents_required.name: Certificate of Landlessness (or verification via KALIA portal)

pros: Bypasses the biggest hurdle for rural credit (land ownership) by using a 'social collateral' JLG model.
Provides up to ₹1.6 Lakh directly to landless groups to lease land, buy seeds, or start agri-allied activities.
cons: Must form a trusted group of 5; if one member defaults, the entire group loses access to future credit.
application_steps: Village-level workers (Krushak Mitras) identify landless farmers and help form JLGs.
Group details are verified against the state's KALIA database.
The JLG applies for a crop loan at the local Primary Agricultural Cooperative Society (PACS) or bank branch.

name: Sharad Pawar Gram Samridhi Yojana
ministry: Employment Guarantee Department, Govt of Maharashtra

poultry_shed.note: Provides ~₹70,000 for constructing a poultry shed and varying amounts for goat sheds and Nadep compost pits.

effective_interest_rate_note: Direct cash support and wage payment for asset construction; no loan required.
eligibility_human: Rural farmers and agricultural laborers in Maharashtra holding a valid MGNREGA job card. To qualify for a cattle shed, the farmer must own at least 2 cows or buffaloes.
pros: Provides nearly ₹77,000 in free cash support (wages + material costs) to build permanent shelters for livestock, directly reducing animal mortality.
Improves farm sanitation and organic fertilizer production through Nadep compost pits.
cons: Tied to MGNREGA wage delays; material cost reimbursement can sometimes take months after construction.
application_steps: Obtain the application form from the Gram Rozgar Sevak at the Gram Panchayat.
Submit the form with job card and animal details.
Gram Sevak provides technical approval; construct the shed.
Subsidy/wages are released in phases based on physical verification of construction.

name: Satat Jivikoparjan Yojana (SJY)
ministry: Rural Development Department, Govt of Bihar
effective_interest_rate_note: 100% non-repayable grant disbursed in phases (Asset, Livelihood Gap Fund, and Capacity Building).
eligibility_human: Ultra-poor households, primarily women from SC/ST and exceptionally vulnerable communities, destitute families, and households formerly engaged in the production of illicit liquor (toddy tappers) transitioning to legal livelihoods.

documents_required.name: Identification via Gram Sabha / Village Organization

pros: Does not require the beneficiary to take on debt. Completely free cash injection to pull families out of extreme poverty.
Includes 7 months of continuous consumption support (Livelihood Gap Fund) while the new business (e.g., goat rearing, petty shop) stabilizes.
cons: Beneficiaries are strictly identified and endorsed by local JEEViKA Village Organizations; one cannot independently apply online.
application_steps: Local Village Organization (VO) and Master Resource Persons conduct a participatory identification of the ultra-poor.
Endorsed households are grouped.
Asset transfer (e.g., purchasing livestock or shop inventory) is facilitated, followed by weekly capacity-building visits.

name: Tribal Development Fund (TDF) - Wadi Model
ministry: NABARD

landless_tribals.note: Landless tribal families are provided micro-enterprise support (e.g., tailoring, leaf plate making, pig/goat rearing) in lieu of orchard development.

effective_interest_rate_note: A highly structured grant provided over a 5 to 7 year period.
eligibility_human: Tribal families holding less than 5 acres of land. A 'Wadi' (small orchard of 1-2 acres) is developed for them. Landless tribals in the project area are included via non-farm micro-enterprise grants.
pros: Turns unproductive wasteland into income-generating orchards (mango, cashew, amla) with full funding for saplings, fencing, and drip irrigation.
Comprehensive wrap-around services including women's health and sanitation components.
cons: Beneficiaries must wait for a Project Implementing Agency (PIA) to launch a project in their specific geography; they cannot apply individually.
application_steps: NABARD sanctions a TDF project to an NGO for a specific tribal block.
The NGO selects 500-1000 tribal families based on landholdings and vulnerability.
Funds are released directly to the Village Level Committee (VLC) to execute the orchard planting and micro-enterprise setups.

name: Namo Drone Didi Scheme
ministry: Ministry of Agriculture & Farmers Welfare
implementing_agency: Lead Fertiliser Companies (LFCs) / State Agri Depts
effective_interest_rate_note: Provides an 80% direct subsidy on drone packages (drones, batteries, cameras). The remaining 20% can be financed via the Agriculture Infrastructure Fund (AIF) at a 3% interest subvention.
eligibility_human: Women Self Help Groups (SHGs) operating in rural clusters. The SHG must nominate a member for a 15-day drone pilot training program to establish an agricultural spraying business.
pros: Massive 80% capital subsidy (up to ₹8 Lakh) to acquire advanced drone technology.
Creates a highly lucrative local business model (renting out drone spraying services to farmers).
cons: Highly selective cluster-based rollout; not universally available to all SHGs immediately.
application_steps: State agencies and LFCs identify viable SHG clusters based on agricultural density.
SHG nominates a member who undergoes DGCA-approved 15-day drone pilot training.
Drone package is supplied, and SHG begins offering commercial spraying services.

contact_info.helpline: Contact Local KVK or Agriculture Department

name: Formation and Promotion of 10,000 FPOs Scheme
ministry: Ministry of Agriculture & Farmers Welfare

credit_guarantee.note: Provides an 85% credit guarantee cover for project loans up to ₹1 Crore, and 75% cover for loans between ₹1 Crore and ₹2 Crore.

effective_interest_rate_note: The scheme provides a matching equity grant (free capital) up to ₹15 Lakh.
eligibility_human: Farmer Producer Organisations (FPOs) registered under the Companies Act or Cooperative Societies Act. Must have a minimum number of farmer members (300 in plains, 100 in NER/Hilly areas).
pros: Doubles the working capital of the FPO instantly by providing a matching equity grant (up to ₹2,000 per farmer member).
Removes collateral requirements for bank loans up to ₹2 Crore.
cons: Management cost support (up to ₹18 Lakh) is routed through the implementing agency, not handed directly to the FPO.
application_steps: FPO collects equity shares from its farmer members.
Apply for the matching Equity Grant through the nodal agency (SFAC/NABARD).
To obtain loans, apply via an eligible lender (commercial bank/NABKISAN) who will secure the backend credit guarantee.

contact_info.helpline: Contact respective CBBO or NABARD DDM

name: Tantya Mama Arthik Kalyan Yojana
ministry: Tribal Affairs Department, MP
effective_interest_rate_note: The state government provides a 7% interest subvention per annum for a maximum of 5 years. It also covers the bank loan guarantee fee.
eligibility_human: Scheduled Tribe (ST) individuals of MP aged 18 to 55 who are NOT income tax payers. Unlike other schemes, there is absolutely no minimum educational qualification required.
pros: Perfect for highly marginalized tribal members starting very small businesses (retail, service) as it requires no educational certificates.
7% subvention almost completely wipes out the real interest burden on the borrower.
cons: The maximum loan limit is strictly capped at ₹1 Lakh.
application_steps: Register via Aadhaar e-KYC on the MP SAMAST Portal.
Fill out the business details and submit to DTIC.
DTIC forwards the application to the bank for collateral-free sanction.

name: Samagra Gavya Vikas Yojana
ministry: Animal and Fisheries Resources Department, Govt of Bihar

ebc_sc_st.note: Incredible 75% capital subsidy on the unit cost for EBC, SC, and ST categories (50% for General/OBC).

effective_interest_rate_note: Direct capital grant applied to the purchase of milch animals (cows/buffaloes) and dairy infrastructure.
eligibility_human: Residents of Bihar aged 18+ looking to establish new dairy farms (units of 2, 4, 15, or 20 milch animals) or related infrastructure.

documents_required.name: Proof of Land/Space for Dairy Shed

pros: One of the highest subsidy rates in the country (75%) for purchasing 2 to 4 milch animals.
Integrates with local milk cooperatives (COMFED/Sudha) for assured milk procurement.
cons: Applicants often need to invest upfront or secure a bank loan before the backend subsidy is released into their account.
application_steps: Register and apply online at the Bihar Dairy portal during the active application window.
Submit land and caste documents.
District Committee selects beneficiaries. After purchasing animals (often via loan), physical verification is done and subsidy is released.

name: Mukhyamantri Yuva Swarojgar Yojana (MYSY)
ministry: Department of MSME & Export Promotion, UP

promoter_contribution.note: General category applicants contribute 10% from their pocket, while SC/ST/OBC/Women/PwD contribute only 5%.

effective_interest_rate_note: Standard bank term loan rates apply. The 25% margin money subsidy heavily reduces the principal loan amount.
eligibility_human: Youth of Uttar Pradesh aged 18 to 40 who have passed at least 10th standard (High School) and are setting up a new manufacturing or service enterprise.
pros: Provides 25% capital subsidy for industry projects up to ₹25 Lakh and service projects up to ₹10 Lakh.
Excellent alternative to PMEGP for UP residents if PMEGP targets are exhausted.
cons: Trading and retail sectors are strictly not eligible.
Must not be a beneficiary of any other central/state self-employment scheme.
application_steps: Apply on the DIUPMSME portal.
DIC Task Force interviews the candidate and forwards the file to a bank.
Bank sanctions the loan and DIC releases the margin money to the bank as a lock-in TDR.

name: SMART (State of Maharashtra’s Agribusiness and Rural Transformation)
ministry: Department of Agriculture, Govt of Maharashtra
effective_interest_rate_note: A direct capital grant (up to 60%) to establish Productive Partnerships (PP) and Market Access Plans (MAP) for agri-value chains.
eligibility_human: Community Based Organizations (CBOs) including FPOs, Cluster Level Federations (CLFs) of SHGs, and Primary Agriculture Credit Societies (PACS) engaging in post-harvest management and value addition.
pros: World Bank-backed project offering massive capital grants up to ₹5 Crore for CBOs to build processing units and warehouses.
Links farmer groups directly with corporate buyers and retail chains.
cons: Highly complex application process requiring a proven track record, corporate buyer MoUs, and an extensive Market Access Plan (MAP).
application_steps: CBO responds to a formal Call for Proposals on the SMART portal.
Submit a Concept Note. If shortlisted, submit a Full Project Proposal (FPP).
CBO deposits its 40% share (own funds + bank loan) into an escrow account.
SMART project releases the 60% grant in tranches based on construction milestones.

name: Kisan Credit Card (KCC) & Modified Interest Subvention Scheme (MISS)
ministry: Ministry of Agriculture & Farmers Welfare / MoF

prompt_repayment.note: Farmers get a 3% Prompt Repayment Incentive (PRI), dropping the effective interest rate from 7% to 4% for loans up to ₹3 Lakh.

animal_husbandry_fisheries.note: Animal husbandry and fisheries farmers can access this 4% rate for short-term working capital up to ₹2 Lakh.

effective_interest_rate_note: Effective interest rate is 4% per annum if repaid within one year of disbursement.
eligibility_human: All farmers, sharecroppers, tenant farmers, JLGs, and SHGs needing short-term credit for crop production, post-harvest expenses, consumption requirements, and maintenance of farm assets.
pros: The absolute cheapest formal credit available in India (4% per annum).
No collateral is required for KCC loans up to ₹1.6 Lakh (sometimes enhanced to ₹3 Lakh tied to crop value).
cons: Must be repaid entirely within 12 months (or the crop cycle) to unlock the 3% PRI; defaulting incurs standard high compound rates.
application_steps: Submit the one-page simplified KCC form to the nearest bank branch.
Bank calculates the scale of finance based on acreage and crop type.
Credit limit is sanctioned and accessible via a RuPay KCC ATM Card.

name: Agricultural Marketing Infrastructure (AMI) sub-scheme of ISAM
ministry: Ministry of Agriculture & Farmers Welfare

sc_st_women_fpo.note: Registered FPOs, SC/ST, Women, and applicants in NER/Hilly areas receive a 33.33% subsidy (up to ₹30 Lakhs for 1000 MT capacity godowns).

effective_interest_rate_note: Direct capital grant applied to the back-end of a term loan.
eligibility_human: Farmers, agri-entrepreneurs, FPOs, Cooperatives, and State Agencies building scientific storage godowns (rural godowns), primary processing centers, or packing infrastructure.

documents_required.name: Detailed Project Report (DPR) approved by Bank
Building Plan Approved by Competent Authority

pros: Massive 25% to 33.33% subsidy on building scientific rural godowns.
Can be converged seamlessly with the Agri Infrastructure Fund (AIF) to stack the 3% interest subvention on top of this capital subsidy.
cons: The godown MUST conform to WDRA (Warehousing Development and Regulatory Authority) engineering specifications to qualify.
application_steps: Draft a WDRA-compliant DPR and secure a bank term loan.
The bank disburses the first installment and claims the advance subsidy from NABARD.
Joint Inspection Committee (JIC) verifies the completed godown before the final subsidy is adjusted.

name: Rajasthan Mahila Nidhi
ministry: Rajasthan Rural Livelihood Project (RGAVP)

interest_subvention.note: State Government provides an 8% interest subvention to loans disbursed under the Nidhi, heavily discounting the borrowing cost.

effective_interest_rate_note: Highly subsidized credit model leveraging a cooperative framework.
eligibility_human: Women who are members of Self-Help Groups (SHGs) affiliated with Rajeevika in Rajasthan.
pros: Ultra-fast processing: Loans up to ₹40,000 are credited to the bank account within 48 hours, and up to ₹1 Lakh within 15 days.
Reduces reliance on exploitative microfinance institutions by using a state-backed cooperative structure.
cons: Exclusive to members of Rajeevika SHGs.
application_steps: SHG drafts an internal micro-credit resolution.
Application is passed through the Cluster Level Federation to the Mahila Nidhi portal digitally.
Instant disbursement directly to the SHG member's account.

name: Dr. Panjabrao Deshmukh Interest Concession Scheme
ministry: Cooperation, Marketing & Textiles Dept, Maharashtra
implementing_agency: District Central Cooperative Banks / Commercial Banks

zero_percent_credit.note: When stacked with the Central Govt's 3% PRI, this scheme effectively drops the interest rate to 0% for crop loans up to ₹3 Lakh for prompt repayers.

effective_interest_rate_note: Borrowers pay 0% interest if the crop loan (up to ₹3 Lakh) is repaid by June 30 of the following year. The state subvents 3% on top of the central 3% PRI.
eligibility_human: All farmers holding land in Maharashtra availing short-term crop loans via KCC from District Central Cooperative Banks (DCCBs), RRBs, or Commercial Banks.
pros: Makes capital entirely free (0% interest) for farmers managing typical acreage.
Process is largely automated at the backend by the PACS and DCCBs.
cons: Missing the June 30 repayment deadline voids the entire state and central subvention, instantly reverting the loan to standard high commercial rates.
application_steps: Borrow short-term crop loan from PACS/Bank.
Repay the entire principal amount out of pocket or via crop sales before June 30.
Bank automatically claims the state and central subvention and nullifies the interest charge.

name: Pradhan Mantri Matsya Kisan Samridhi Sah-Yojana (PM-MKSSY)
ministry: Ministry of Fisheries, Animal Husbandry & Dairying

sc_st_women_ffpo.note: Performance grant jumps to 35% of total investment for SC, ST, Women-owned microenterprises (max ₹45 Lakhs), and 35% for Fish FPOs (max ₹200 Lakhs).

effective_interest_rate_note: Provides backend performance grants based on job creation and infrastructure development. Also provides a 40% subsidy on aquaculture insurance premiums.
eligibility_human: Fishers, Fish Farmer Producer Organizations (FFPOs), Micro & Small enterprises operating in the fisheries sector (processing, ice plants, aquaculture).

documents_required.name: Detailed Project Report for Infra Upgrade
Proof of Job Creation (EPFO/Payroll) for claims

pros: Rewards formalization: For every job created/maintained (woman), ₹15,000/year is paid as a grant.
Massive ₹2 Crore grant upper limit for FFPOs building supply chain infrastructure.
cons: Complex compliance burden (requires formal payroll tracking and National Fisheries Digital Platform registration to claim grants).
application_steps: Register on the National Fisheries Digital Platform (NFDP).
Invest in capital plant/machinery or establish formalized payroll.
Submit audited proofs of investment and employment to NFDB for performance grant release.

name: Per Drop More Crop (PDMC) - Micro Irrigation
ministry: Ministry of Agriculture & Farmers Welfare

general_category.note: 45% subsidy for other (General) farmers. State governments often add top-up subsidies, pushing total coverage to 70-90% in states like Maharashtra/Gujarat.

effective_interest_rate_note: Direct backend subsidy on the invoice of the micro-irrigation system.
eligibility_human: All farmers possessing agricultural land. Small and Marginal Farmers (less than 2 hectares) get priority 55% central share.
pros: Massive reduction in installation cost of Drip and Sprinkler systems, leading to a 30-50% increase in crop yield and fertilizer efficiency.
Most states have dedicated portals (e.g., e-Thibak) to process this instantly.
cons: Farmers must strictly purchase hardware from a list of government-empanelled manufacturers.
application_steps: Farmer registers on the state's agriculture DBT portal.
Selects an empanelled manufacturer and uploads land details.
State generates an approval order; vendor installs the system.
Post physical verification with geo-tagging, the subsidy is released directly to the vendor/farmer account.

name: National Bamboo Mission (NBM)
ministry: Ministry of Agriculture & Farmers Welfare

government_agencies.note: 100% funding is provided for government agencies establishing nurseries.

effective_interest_rate_note: Direct capital grant covering 50% of the unit cost for private entrepreneurs establishing nurseries, treatment plants, and product units.
eligibility_human: Farmers, artisans, FPOs, Cooperatives, and private entrepreneurs looking to set up Bamboo nurseries, plantations, primary processing units, or handicraft micro-units.
pros: Offers up to ₹25 Lakhs per unit (50% of ₹50 Lakh norm) for setting up bamboo processing units (making agarbatti sticks, furniture, bamboo boards).
Excellent support for establishing high-tech tissue culture nurseries.
cons: Heavily reliant on the proactivity of the respective State Bamboo Mission to release funds.
application_steps: Draft a proposal matching the NBM operational guidelines unit costs.
Submit the proposal to the District Level Agency / State Bamboo Mission.
Once approved by the State Level Executive Committee (SLEC), funds are released in milestones.

name: GOBARdhan / SATAT (Compressed Bio Gas)
ministry: Ministry of Drinking Water & Sanitation / MNRE
effective_interest_rate_note: A massive direct grant (Central Financial Assistance) provided per project, rather than a percentage of the loan.
eligibility_human: Entrepreneurs, FPOs, and Corporates setting up medium-to-large Compressed Bio Gas (CBG) or Bio-CNG plants utilizing cattle dung and agricultural waste.
pros: Grants up to ₹4 Crore per 12,000 cum/day CBG plant, significantly reducing CAPEX.
SATAT scheme guarantees long-term offtake of the produced CBG by state oil companies, ensuring assured revenue.
cons: Requires massive upfront capital, complex engineering, and strict environmental clearances.
application_steps: Submit an Expression of Interest (EoI) on the SATAT portal.
Obtain an LOI from an Oil Marketing Company.
Secure project financing (often via AIF) and apply for CFA through MNRE/IREDA.
Subsidy is released after successful commissioning and continuous operation.

name: New Entrepreneur-cum-Enterprise Development Scheme (NEEDS)
ministry: Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises Department, Govt of Tamil Nadu

interest_subvention.note: A 3% interest subvention is provided throughout the entire repayment tenure of the bank loan.

effective_interest_rate_note: Bank lending rate reduced by 3% per annum through state interest subvention, combined with an upfront 25% capital subsidy.
eligibility_human: Educated youth aged 21-35 (relaxed up to 45 for SC, ST, MBC, BC, Women, PwD, and Transgender candidates) who possess a Degree, Diploma, or ITI certificate, establishing a new enterprise in Tamil Nadu.
pros: 25% direct capital subsidy capped at ₹75 Lakh with a project cost scale up to ₹5 Crore.
Integrated 3% interest subvention for the complete repayment lifecycle.
Includes mandatory EDP training by Entrepreneurship Development and Innovation Institute (EDII).
cons: Excludes all trading and commercial retail ventures.
Applicants must not have previously benefited from central or state capital subsidy schemes.
application_steps: Apply online on the Tamil Nadu MSME portal.
District Task Force Committee interviews and shortlists candidates.
Complete 25-day EDP training program conducted by EDII.
Bank/TIIC sanctions loan; DIC deposits 25% subsidy into escrow account.

name: Unemployed Youth Employment Generation Programme (UYEGP)
ministry: Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises Department, Govt of Tamil Nadu

promoter_contribution.note: Special category candidates (SC/ST/BC/MBC/Women/Minorities/Differently Abled) contribute only 5% promoter equity; General category contributes 10%.

effective_interest_rate_note: Standard commercial bank lending rates apply. Government provides 25% margin money subsidy directly reducing the debt burden.
eligibility_human: Residents of Tamil Nadu aged 18-35 (relaxed to 45 for SC/ST/BC/MBC/Women/PwD) having minimum 8th standard pass and annual family income not exceeding ₹5,00,000.
pros: Permits trading ventures up to ₹5 Lakh, service up to ₹5 Lakh, and manufacturing up to ₹15 Lakh.
Low barrier to entry with minimum qualification of only 8th standard pass.
Low promoter equity contribution of only 5% for reserved classes.
cons: Strict family annual income cap of ₹5 Lakh.
Subsidy is kept in a Term Deposit Receipt (TDR) for 3 years before final adjustment.
application_steps: Submit application on the online UYEGP portal.
Appear before the District Level Task Force Committee for personal interview.
Selected applications are forwarded to candidate's preferred bank branch.
Complete 7-day EDP training after loan sanction to trigger subsidy disbursement.

name: Annal Ambedkar Business Champions Scheme (AABCS)
ministry: Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises Department, Govt of Tamil Nadu

interest_subvention.note: Provides a 6% interest subvention for the entire loan repayment period.

effective_interest_rate_note: A 6% interest subvention directly deducted from bank term loan interest rates, combined with an upfront 35% capital subsidy.
eligibility_human: Scheduled Caste (SC) and Scheduled Tribe (ST) entrepreneurs of Tamil Nadu aged 18 to 55 setting up greenfield units or modernizing/expanding existing units in manufacturing, service, or commercial transport sectors.
pros: Industry-leading 35% capital subsidy capped up to ₹75 Lakh.
Exceptional 6% interest subvention for the total loan period.
Covers commercial vehicle purchases and expansions of existing running units.
cons: Exclusive strictly to SC and ST entrepreneurs.
At least 51% proprietary ownership must remain with SC/ST members throughout tenure.
application_steps: Apply online at the official AABCS web portal.
District Task Force Committee reviews and accords provisional recommendation.
Empanelled bank or TIIC sanctions loan facilities.
Capital subsidy disbursed directly to beneficiary loan account as back-ended deposit.

name: Chief Minister Employment Generation Programme (CMEGP Karnataka)
ministry: Commerce and Industries Department, Govt of Karnataka

sc_st_women_rural.note: General category gets 25% in urban and 30% in rural areas. SC, ST, OBC, Minorities, Women, and Rural units receive up to 35% capital subsidy.

effective_interest_rate_note: Standard bank lending rates apply. Government provides back-ended margin money subsidy to lower the borrower principal repayment.
eligibility_human: Residents of Karnataka aged 21-45 (relaxed up to 50 for SC/ST/Women/Minorities/Ex-Servicemen) establishing a new manufacturing or service micro-enterprise.
pros: Generous capital subsidy up to 35% on projects costing up to ₹1 Crore for manufacturing.
Service sector ventures funded up to ₹50 Lakh.
Low promoter equity contribution of 5% for backward classes and women.
cons: Pure trading, retail, and commercial goods transportation are ineligible.
Margin money locked in TDR for 3 years before credit to loan account.
application_steps: Submit online application via the Karnataka CMEGP web portal.
District Level Task Force Committee interviews candidate.
Application transmitted online to selected commercial bank branch.
Loan disbursed and state subsidy deposited directly to beneficiary bank branch as TDR.

name: Karnataka ELEVATE 100 Startup Grant Scheme
ministry: Department of Electronics, IT, BT and S&T, Govt of Karnataka

kalyana_karnataka_and_women.note: Special ELEVATE cohorts operate with ring-fenced funds dedicated to Women founders, OBC/SC/ST entrepreneurs, and Kalyana Karnataka region startups.

effective_interest_rate_note: 100% non-dilutive grant-in-aid disbursed in milestone-based tranches. No equity or repayment required.
eligibility_human: Startups registered in Karnataka incorporated as Private Limited or LLP with innovative tech/intellectual property. Startup must be registered on the Startup Karnataka portal.
pros: Up to ₹50 Lakh pure non-dilutive grant with zero equity dilution.
Access to Government of Karnataka venture networks, lab facilities, and subsidized cloud credits.
Exemption from prior turnover and experience criteria in state public procurement.
cons: Highly selective multi-tier pitching evaluation with low acceptance rates.
Disbursements strictly tied to rigorous technical audit and validation of expenditure.
application_steps: Register company on the Startup Karnataka portal.
Submit application and pitch presentation during call for ELEVATE cohort.
Participate in regional pitch round and Grand Jury evaluation.
Sign Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) with KITS and unlock milestone tranches.

name: Telangana State Program for Rapid Incubation of Dalit Entrepreneurs (T-PRIDE)
ministry: Industries and Commerce Department, Govt of Telangana

women_sc_st.note: SC and ST Women entrepreneurs receive an enhanced investment subsidy of 45% on fixed capital investment up to ₹75 Lakh.

power_and_interest.note: 100% reimbursement of stamp duty, ₹1.50 per unit power subsidy for 5 years, and 9% interest subvention on term loans for 5 years.

effective_interest_rate_note: A 9% interest subvention per annum on term loans for 5 years, reducing borrowing rates down to near zero or nominal margins.
eligibility_human: Scheduled Caste (SC), Scheduled Tribe (ST), and Differently Abled (PHC) entrepreneurs setting up micro and small manufacturing units or commercial transport enterprises in Telangana.
pros: 35% to 45% direct investment subsidy on plant and machinery up to ₹75 Lakh.
High 9% interest subvention per annum for 5 years.
Includes commercial taxi and freight vehicle financing under transport sector.
cons: 100% SC/ST/PwD ownership required; non-SC/ST equity dilution cancels benefits.
Claims processed after commencement of commercial production.
application_steps: Acquire statutory clearance via TS-iPASS single-window portal.
Secure term loan financing and execute plant construction.
Apply for incentives on TS-iPASS within 6 months of commencing operations.
District and State Level Committees inspect and sanction subsidy claims directly to bank account.

name: Telangana State Industrial Development and Entrepreneur Advancement (T-IDEA)
ministry: Industries and Commerce Department, Govt of Telangana

women_entrepreneurs.note: Women entrepreneurs receive an enhanced 20% capital subsidy on fixed capital investment up to ₹25 Lakh.

interest_subvention.note: A 3% interest rebate on term loans for up to 5 years for Micro and Small Enterprises.

effective_interest_rate_note: A 3% interest subvention for Micro/Small units, combined with 100% stamp duty reimbursement and 50% net SGST reimbursement for 5 years.
eligibility_human: General and OBC entrepreneurs setting up greenfield manufacturing enterprises or undertaking substantial expansion in Telangana.

documents_required.name: Chartered Accountant Certificate of Plant Investment

pros: 15% to 20% capital subsidy on machinery and building assets.
100% reimbursement of stamp duty and transfer duty paid on land purchase/lease.
Reimbursement of 50% net SGST paid for 5 years from production date.
cons: Does not cover trading, service units, or transport businesses.
Subsidies are released post-commissioning based on budget releases.
application_steps: Register enterprise clearances through TS-iPASS single-window system.
Commission manufacturing unit within stipulated project timeline.
File claim for T-IDEA incentives online via TS-iPASS within 6 months of commercial launch.
Physical verification by District Industries Centre followed by state treasury disbursement.

name: YSR Cheyutha Scheme
ministry: Department of Social Welfare, Govt of Andhra Pradesh
implementing_agency: SERP / MEPMA / Andhra Pradesh State Housing Corporation

commercial_linkages.note: Beneficiaries receive technical tie-ups and direct supply chain tie-ups with corporate giants (Amul, ITC, HUL, P&G) to set up grocery or dairy micro-businesses.

effective_interest_rate_note: Direct financial aid of ₹75,000 paid across four equal annual installments of ₹18,750. Eligible for commercial bank credit linkages for business expansion.
eligibility_human: Women residents of Andhra Pradesh aged 45 to 60 belonging to SC, ST, BC, and Minority communities with rural household monthly income below ₹10,000 (urban below ₹12,000).
pros: Direct grant of ₹75,000 transferred with zero debt liability.
Comprehensive livelihood support to launch kirana shops, dairy micro-units, or sheep units with corporate supply chain tie-ups.
Bypasses complex bank appraisals for base grant capital.
cons: Strict age bracket restricted to 45-60 years.
Disbursed in 4 annual tranches rather than a single upfront capital lump sum.
application_steps: Enroll through the local Village/Ward Volunteer at Grama Sachivalayam.
Social audit verification by Village Secretariat Welfare Assistant.
Beneficiary list published on Navasakam portal.
Funds credited directly via DBT to Aadhaar-enabled bank account.

name: Mukhyamantri Mahila Utkarsh Yojana (MMUY)
ministry: Women and Child Development Department, Govt of Gujarat
effective_interest_rate_note: 100% interest-free loan (0% interest). The State Government bears the full bank interest rate and stamp duty charges.
eligibility_human: Women in Gujarat who form a Joint Liability and Earning Group (JLEG) comprising 10 women members. Group must open an operative bank account for micro-enterprise operations.

documents_required.name: JLEG Group Resolution and Bank Passbook

pros: Completely interest-free loan up to ₹1,00,000 per 10-woman group.
Stamp duty waived completely by the state government.
Zero collateral required; operates under group mutual guarantee.
cons: Requires collective consensus of 10 women; mutual liability applies if one member defaults.
Short repayment duration of 12 equal monthly installments.
application_steps: Mobilize 10 women to form a Joint Liability Earning Group (JLEG).
Get group recognized by urban local body (GULM) or rural mission (GLPC).
Apply to partner bank branch with KYC and loan resolution.
Bank disburses ₹1,00,000 to group account; state remits interest to bank.

name: Manav Kalyan Yojana Gujarat
ministry: Cottage and Rural Industries Department, Govt of Gujarat
implementing_agency: Commissioner of Cottage and Rural Industries / DIC
effective_interest_rate_note: 100% free physical toolkits and machinery equipment provided directly by the state government; no loan liability.
eligibility_human: Artisans, rural laborers, and micro self-employed individuals in Gujarat aged 16-60 working across 28 approved trades (e.g., masonry, tailoring, carpentry, barber, cobbler) with rural family income under ₹1,20,000 (urban under ₹1,50,000).

documents_required.name: Trade Experience Certificate or Vocational Training Proof

pros: Provides premium, brand-new professional equipment/toolkits without any financial borrowing.
Covers 28 distinct traditional, artisan, and localized vocation trades.
Seamless paperless verification through e-Kutir web portal.
cons: Strict income ceilings exclude lower-middle-class entrepreneurs.
Physical tool distribution happens at district events, occasionally causing delivery backlogs.
application_steps: Register an account on the e-Kutir Gujarat online platform.
Select trade and upload Aadhaar, income, and trade verification.
Scrutiny by District Cottage Industries Officer.
Receive physical toolkit at designated Taluka distribution camp.

name: Kerala Entrepreneur Support Scheme (ESS)
ministry: Department of Industries and Commerce, Govt of Kerala
