Saplings and fencing materials are provided free of cost.
Beneficiary receives wages for planting and maintaining their own orchard over 3 years.

name: Phulo Jhano Ashirwad Abhiyan
ministry: Rural Development Department, Govt of Jharkhand
effective_interest_rate_note: Initial ₹10,000 is an interest-free loan/grant to start a respectable livelihood. Follow-up larger loans via SHGs are highly subsidized.
eligibility_human: Rural women in Jharkhand who are currently engaged in the manufacturing or selling of illicit liquor (Haria/Daru) and wish to transition to respectable alternative livelihoods (e.g., livestock, retail).
pros: Direct intervention to pull women out of exploitative and illegal liquor trades.
Provides immediate interest-free capital of ₹10,000 without collateral to set up a dignified business.
cons: Strictly targeted rehabilitation scheme; not open to the general public.
application_steps: Village SHGs (Sakhi Mandals) conduct a survey to identify eligible women.
Identified women are counseled and integrated into the SHG network.
An interest-free fund of ₹10,000 is transferred immediately to start an alternative business (like poultry or grocery).

name: Bihar Krishi Yantra Subsidy Yojana
ministry: Agriculture Department, Govt of Bihar

ebc_sc_st.note: EBC, SC, and ST farmers receive up to 80% subsidy on selected farm machinery (e.g., rotavators, reapers, threshers).

effective_interest_rate_note: Direct backend subsidy on the purchase of agricultural machinery.
eligibility_human: Farmers in Bihar possessing valid land possession certificates or updated rent receipts. Covers over 100 types of farm machinery.
pros: Subsidizes up to 80% for marginalized communities on crucial machinery.
Fully digital application and permit generation system.
cons: Farmers must purchase machinery strictly from state-approved vendors, which sometimes restricts choices.
application_steps: Register on the DBT Agriculture Bihar portal.
Apply on the OFMAS (Online Farm Mechanization Application System) portal for the specific machine.
Receive online permit/approval.
Purchase the machine, upload the bill, and subsidy is transferred directly to the bank account.

name: Mukhyamantri Vriksh Sampada Yojana
ministry: Forest and Climate Change Department, Govt of Chhattisgarh

large_landholdings.note: 100% financial assistance is given for planting on up to 5 acres of land. For planting between 5 acres and 500 acres, 50% financial assistance is provided.

effective_interest_rate_note: A pure financial grant disbursed annually for 3 years to cover plantation and maintenance costs.
eligibility_human: Farmers, Gram Panchayats, private companies, and institutions in Chhattisgarh holding private land and willing to plant commercial tree species (e.g., Tissue Culture Bamboo, Eucalyptus, Teak, Sandalwood).
pros: Guaranteed purchase of the harvested timber by the state government or empanelled private companies.
100% cost coverage for up to 5 acres, making it extremely lucrative for small landholders to utilize barren land.
cons: Commitment is long-term (trees take 3-10 years to mature), locking up land from seasonal crop cycles.
application_steps: Submit application form to the local Forest Range Officer.
Forest department surveys the land and provides appropriate saplings.
Farmer plants the trees; department verifies survival rates annually.
Financial assistance is released to the bank account over 3 years.

name: Pashudhan Kisan Credit Card Scheme
ministry: Animal Husbandry & Dairying Department, Govt of Haryana

interest_subvention.note: Combined with 3% Central subvention, the State Govt provides a 4% interest subvention, making the working capital loan (up to ₹3 Lakh) completely 0% interest for prompt repayers.

effective_interest_rate_note: 0% effective interest rate for loans up to ₹3 Lakh if repaid within one year. Collateral-free up to ₹1.6 Lakh.
eligibility_human: Animal rearers and farmers in Haryana owning livestock (cows, buffaloes, sheep, goats, pigs, poultry). The loan amount is fixed per animal (e.g., ₹60,249 per buffalo, ₹40,783 per cow).

documents_required.name: Animal Health Certificate & Ear Tag Number

pros: Provides entirely interest-free working capital for buying fodder, medicine, and maintaining livestock.
Loan limits are clearly quantified per animal, removing bank appraisal ambiguity.
cons: If the loan is not repaid within 1 year, the farmer loses the 7% total subvention and must pay standard interest (approx. 9-11%).
application_steps: Get animals examined and ear-tagged at the local veterinary hospital.
Veterinary surgeon issues an animal health certificate.
Submit application form with the certificate to the bank.
Bank issues the Pashudhan KCC allowing withdrawal of funds as needed.

name: Mera Pani Meri Virasat
ministry: Agriculture & Farmers Welfare Department, Govt of Haryana

agroforestry.note: Farmers planting trees (agroforestry) instead of paddy receive ₹10,000 per acre per year for 3 years.

effective_interest_rate_note: A direct cash grant per acre to offset the income drop from switching crops. No loan involved.
eligibility_human: Farmers in Haryana (especially in specified water-depleted blocks) who voluntarily switch from water-intensive paddy (rice) cultivation to alternative crops like maize, cotton, millet, pulses, or horticulture.
pros: Guarantees a financial cushion (₹7,000 per acre) while diversifying crops, reducing ground-water depletion.
Fully integrated with the state procurement system (crops like maize and bajra are procured at MSP).
cons: Strict monitoring; if satellite imaging/physical surveys detect paddy cultivation, the grant is withheld.
application_steps: Register the farm acreage and crop plan on the 'Meri Fasal Mera Byora' portal before sowing.
Cultivate the alternative crop (maize, pulses, etc.).
Agriculture department conducts field verification during the season.
The grant of ₹7,000 per acre is transferred via DBT in two installments.

name: Prakritik Kheti Khushhal Kisan Yojana (PK3Y)
ministry: Agriculture Department, Govt of Himachal Pradesh

desi_cow_purchase.note: Provides 50% subsidy (up to ₹25,000) for purchasing indigenous (Desi) cows essential for natural farming formulations.

effective_interest_rate_note: Direct backend subsidy on the purchase of inputs for natural farming. No loan required.
eligibility_human: Farmers in Himachal Pradesh willing to adopt Subhash Palekar Natural Farming (SPNF) techniques, eliminating chemical fertilizers and pesticides.
pros: Subsidizes 75% of the cost for plastic drums (used to prepare Jeevamrutha) and lining materials.
Provides financial support to buy indigenous cows, which are the backbone of natural farming.
Reduces overall farming costs drastically by eliminating chemical purchases.
cons: Transitioning to natural farming yields can be slow in the first 1-2 years.
application_steps: Register with the local ATMA block officer.
Undergo mandatory training in Subhash Palekar Natural Farming methodologies.
Purchase required materials (drums, cows) and submit bills to ATMA.
Subsidy is credited via DBT to the farmer's account.

name: Mukhya Mantri Krishi Sa-Sajuli Yojna
ministry: Agriculture Department, Govt of Assam
effective_interest_rate_note: A pure direct cash transfer of ₹5,000 intended for farm tools. No loan or repayment involved.
eligibility_human: Small and marginal farmers of Assam (owning more than 1 Bigha but less than 2 Hectares) and active tenant farmers. Minimum age of 21 years.

documents_required.name: Land Patta / Tenant Certification by Gaon Burha

pros: Direct DBT transfer of ₹5,000 gives farmers autonomy to purchase the specific hand-tools or implements they need.
Tenant farmers (who often lack land titles) are eligible with simple certification from the village head.
cons: Only one beneficiary per family is allowed.
A relatively small amount, suitable only for hand tools rather than motorized machinery.
application_steps: Collect application form from the local Agriculture Extension Assistant (AEA).
Submit the filled form along with bank details and land/tenant proof to the AEA.
District Level Committee approves the beneficiary list.
₹5,000 is directly credited to the bank account via DBT.

name: Meghalaya Piggery Mission
ministry: Animal Husbandry & Veterinary Department, Govt of Meghalaya

interest_subvention.note: The state government provides 100% interest subvention. Borrowers repay only the principal amount.

effective_interest_rate_note: 100% interest subvention means the loan is completely interest-free for the borrower, provided EMIs are paid on time.
eligibility_human: Individual farmers, SHGs, and Primary Agricultural Cooperative Societies (PACS) in rural Meghalaya interested in pig breeding and fattening.
pros: 0% interest capital to scale up pig breeding, a highly lucrative market in the North East.
The mission provides high-yield piglets and veterinary support directly.
cons: Borrower must bear the insurance cost of the livestock.
application_steps: Submit application to the local AH & Veterinary Officer.
Officers inspect the proposed site for the pig shed.
Bank sanctions the loan; funds are released directly to empanelled suppliers for piglets and feed.
State government pays the interest component directly to the bank.

name: Mukhyamantri Rubber Mission
ministry: Tribal Welfare Department / Forest Department, Govt of Tripura
effective_interest_rate_note: A 100% financial grant per hectare to establish and maintain rubber plantations over a 5-year gestation period.
eligibility_human: Rural landowners and tribal families in Tripura holding at least 0.5 hectares (approx 1.2 acres) of unutilized or degraded land suitable for rubber plantation.

documents_required.name: Land Patta / Forest Rights Act (FRA) Patta

pros: Fully covers the cost of clearing land, buying rubber stumps, and applying fertilizers for 5 years.
Transforms degraded tribal land into highly lucrative long-term latex-producing assets.
cons: Gestation period is long; rubber trees take 5-7 years before they begin yielding latex/income.
application_steps: Apply through the local TRPC center or Rubber Board field office.
Officials conduct land suitability testing.
Saplings/stumps are provided, and planting is executed.
Maintenance grant is transferred annually to the beneficiary's bank account based on the survival rate of the trees.

name: Mukhyamantri Ghasyari Kalyan Yojana
ministry: Cooperative Department, Govt of Uttarakhand
effective_interest_rate_note: A direct price subsidy. Nutritional cattle feed/fodder is sold to women at ₹2 per kg (heavily subsidized from the market rate).
eligibility_human: Rural women (Ghasyaris) in the hilly districts of Uttarakhand who traditionally spend hours trekking into forests to cut fodder for livestock.
pros: Drastically reduces the physical burden and risk of animal attacks on women collecting forest fodder.
Nutritional silage blocks increase milk yield by 15-20%.
cons: Availability depends strictly on the supply chain efficiency of local PACS.
application_steps: Register at the local Primary Agriculture Credit Society (PACS).
Purchase the 25kg or 30kg vacuum-packed silage blocks at the subsidized rate directly from the cooperative outlet.

name: Telangana State Micro Irrigation Project (TSMIP)
ministry: Agriculture Department, Govt of Telangana

sc_st_farmers.note: 100% free micro-irrigation systems for SC and ST farmers. BC farmers get 90%, and General category farmers get 80% subsidy (up to 5 hectares).

effective_interest_rate_note: Direct capital backend subsidy on the installation invoice.
eligibility_human: Farmers in Telangana owning agricultural land with a viable water source (borewell/open well). Highly subsidized to encourage drip and sprinkler irrigation.
pros: Provides drip/sprinkler systems entirely free (100% subsidy) to SC/ST farmers.
Reduces water consumption by 50% while improving crop yields.
cons: Must purchase the equipment exclusively from government-empanelled MI companies.
application_steps: Apply through the nearest MeeSeva center with land documents and crop details.
Mandal Horticulture Officer conducts a field feasibility survey.
Beneficiary deposits the non-subsidized portion (if applicable) as a DD.
Empanelled vendor installs the system; government pays the vendor the subsidy directly.

name: YSR Rythu Bharosa - PM KISAN
ministry: Agriculture Department, Govt of AP

landless_sc_st_bc.note: Landless tenant farmers and ROFR cultivators belonging to SC, ST, BC, and Minority categories also receive the full ₹13,500 annually (funded entirely by the state, without the PM-KISAN component).

effective_interest_rate_note: A pure direct cash transfer scheme for agricultural investment support.
eligibility_human: All landholding farmer families in AP. Additionally, landless tenant farmers cultivating at least 1 acre (0.5 acres for horticulture) from SC/ST/BC/Minority categories are eligible.

documents_required.name: Crop Cultivation Rights Card (CCRC) for Tenants

pros: Provides ₹13,500 annually (stacked with PM-KISAN) in three installments to meet sowing and harvesting expenses.
One of the few schemes nationally that legally recognizes and funds landless tenant farmers.
cons: Excludes institutional landholders, tax-paying professionals, and government employees.
application_steps: Village volunteers conduct door-to-door surveys to identify cultivators.
Data is cross-verified with Webland and e-Crop portals.
Final eligible lists are displayed at the Grama Sachivalayam.
Funds are released via DBT directly to the Aadhaar-linked bank account.

name: Krushak Assistance for Livelihood and Income Augmentation (KALIA)
ministry: Department of Agriculture and Farmers' Empowerment, Govt of Odisha

landless_households.note: Landless agricultural households receive a one-time grant of ₹12,500 to start allied activities like goat rearing, poultry, or mushroom cultivation. Vulnerable/Elderly landless get ₹10,000/year sustenance.

effective_interest_rate_note: A pure direct cash transfer. Small/Marginal farmers receive ₹4,000 annually (converged with PM-KISAN).
eligibility_human: Small/marginal farmers, landless agricultural laborers, and vulnerable farm families in Odisha. Must not be income tax payers or government employees.
pros: Incredibly inclusive: provides heavy upfront capital (₹12,500) specifically to the landless poor who cannot normally access farm loans.
Includes a robust life insurance (₹2 Lakh) and accident insurance component.
cons: The ongoing annual input assistance for farmers was reduced from ₹10,000 to ₹4,000 to converge with PM-KISAN.
application_steps: Submit the 'Green Form' at the Gram Panchayat office during application phases.
Nodal officers conduct ground verification and cross-check with databases.
Approved lists are finalized and funds transferred directly via DBT.

name: Mukhyamantri Janjati Jeevika Mission (MJJM)
ministry: ST & SC Development, Minorities & Backward Classes Welfare Department
implementing_agency: Tribal Development Cooperative Corporation of Odisha (TDCCOL)
effective_interest_rate_note: A 100% financial grant to improve tribal livelihoods. No loan is required.
eligibility_human: Scheduled Tribe (ST) households residing in the 119 Tribal Sub-Plan (TSP) blocks of Odisha. Focuses on promoting agro-forestry, minor forest produce processing, and livestock rearing.
pros: Provides end-to-end support: from free saplings and goats to setting up processing machinery for Sal leaves/tamarind.
Protects tribal communities from middlemen by funding collective storage and processing infrastructure.
cons: Strictly limited to designated tribal blocks (TSP areas) in the state.
application_steps: Local ITDA officials and NGOs conduct micro-planning at the village level.
Beneficiaries are grouped into producer groups or individual clusters.
Assets (livestock, seeds, processing tools) and capacity building are delivered directly to the village.

name: Bihan (Chhattisgarh State Rural Livelihoods Mission)
ministry: Panchayat and Rural Development Department, Govt of Chhattisgarh

revolving_fund.note: A pure grant of ₹15,000 (Revolving Fund) and up to ₹60,000 (Community Investment Fund) is provided directly to the SHG.

effective_interest_rate_note: Through bank linkages and state interest subvention, SHGs can borrow at incredibly low rates (effective 3% or lower for prompt repayment).
eligibility_human: Rural women in Chhattisgarh organized into Self Help Groups (SHGs) under the Bihan network, having completed 3 to 6 months of regular savings and meetings.
pros: Provides initial non-repayable seed capital to build the group's financial foundation.
Facilitates highly subsidized large-ticket bank loans (Cash Credit limits) without collateral.
cons: Individuals cannot apply; funds must be routed through the collective SHG structure.
application_steps: Women form a 10-15 member group with the help of Community Resource Persons (CRPs).
After 3 months of internal saving, the group receives a ₹15,000 Revolving Fund grant.
After grading, the group prepares a Micro Credit Plan and is linked to a bank for term loans/cash credit.

contact_info.helpline: Contact Local Bihan Block Mission Manager

name: Mukhyamantri Gopalak Yojana
ministry: Animal Husbandry Department, Govt of UP
effective_interest_rate_note: A commercial term loan up to ₹9 Lakh is subsidized by a margin money grant of ₹10,000 per animal (up to ₹90,000) deposited directly by the state over 5 years.
eligibility_human: Unemployed youth in Uttar Pradesh with an annual family income below ₹1 Lakh, looking to set up a dairy unit of 10-20 cows/buffaloes. Must own or lease land for a cattle shed.
pros: Reduces initial capital barrier for setting up mid-scale dairy farms.
The cattle are purchased from state-organized cattle fairs, ensuring quality breeds.
cons: The subsidy is not upfront; it is released in installments of ₹18,000 per year directly to the bank account.
Strict income threshold of ₹1 Lakh restricts many applicants.
application_steps: Submit application to the nearest veterinary hospital or CVO.
District level committee reviews and forwards to a commercial bank.
Bank sanctions the ₹9 Lakh loan.
Applicant purchases 10 animals in Phase 1 and 10 in Phase 2; state releases annual margin money.

name: Mukhyamantri Pashudhan Vikas Yojana
ministry: Animal Husbandry and Dairying Department, MP

sc_st_women.note: SC, ST, and Women beneficiaries receive an enhanced 75% subsidy for establishing poultry, goat, and pig rearing units.

effective_interest_rate_note: A direct capital grant applied to the unit cost of establishing livestock farms. No mandatory bank loan required if self-funded.
eligibility_human: Residents of Madhya Pradesh wishing to start small livestock units (Goat rearing - 10+1 unit, Poultry - Kadaknath/Backyard, Piggery).
pros: Massive 75% subsidy for marginalized groups makes entering livestock rearing virtually risk-free.
Specifically promotes the indigenous and highly profitable 'Kadaknath' poultry breed.
cons: Stock availability depends on state-run hatcheries and breeding farms, which may cause delays.
application_steps: Submit application to the local veterinary surgeon or Deputy Director's office.
Deposit the beneficiary share (25% or 50% via DD).
Department supplies the livestock unit (animals, initial feed, and vaccines) directly.

name: Mukhyamantri Kisan Mitra Urja Yojana
ministry: Energy Department, Govt of Rajasthan
effective_interest_rate_note: A direct tariff subsidy applied to the agricultural electricity bill. No loan involved.
eligibility_human: Metered agricultural power consumers (farmers) in Rajasthan. Employees of central/state governments and income taxpayers are strictly excluded.
pros: Provides a flat subsidy of ₹1,000 per month (₹12,000 annually) directly adjusting the electricity bill, effectively making electricity free for small farmers.
cons: Subsidy is only credited if there are no previous outstanding power dues on the meter.
application_steps: Link Aadhaar and bank account to the DISCOM agricultural connection.
Clear any outstanding historical power dues.
The DISCOM automatically deducts ₹1,000 from the bi-monthly generated bill. Any surplus subsidy is adjusted in the next billing cycle.

name: Ganga Kalyana Scheme
ministry: Minorities Welfare / Backward Classes Welfare Department, Govt of Karnataka
implementing_agency: KMDC / D. Devaraj Urs Backward Classes Development Corporation

community_irrigation.note: For community irrigation (8-15 acres), the unit cost is fully subsidized up to ₹6 Lakhs.

effective_interest_rate_note: The scheme provides a massive ₹4.25 Lakh subsidy. A nominal ₹50,000 loan component is charged at 4% interest per annum.
eligibility_human: Small and marginal farmers from SC, ST, OBC, or Minority communities in Karnataka owning at least 1.5 acres of dry land (1 acre in specific coastal/hilly districts). Rural family income must be under ₹98,000.
pros: Provides end-to-end free irrigation: drills the borewell, supplies the pump set, and manages electrification with ESCOMs.
Maximum unit cost ceiling is very high (up to ₹4.75 Lakh in Bangalore/Kolar regions).
cons: Strict income ceilings exclude middle-income farmers.
Requires farmers to navigate multiple bureaucratic levels (Revenue Dept for land, ESCOMs for power).
application_steps: Apply online via the Seva Sindhu portal or nearest Grama One center.
Upload caste, income, and RTC documents.
Corporation physically verifies the dry land.
Empanelled contractors drill the borewell directly; farmer pays only the nominal loan EMI later.

name: Bhavantar Bharpayee Yojana (BBY)
ministry: Agriculture & Farmers Welfare Department, Govt of Haryana
effective_interest_rate_note: A direct cash compensation scheme. The state pays the difference between the fixed base price and the lower market selling price.
eligibility_human: Horticulture farmers (landlords, lessees, or tenants) in Haryana cultivating specified crops (Tomato, Potato, Onion, Cauliflower).
pros: Shields farmers from devastating market crashes for perishable vegetables.
Ensures a guaranteed minimum income of ₹48,000 to ₹56,000 per acre.
cons: Compensation is entirely dependent on selling the crop officially through HSAMB mandis and securing a 'J-Form'.
application_steps: Register the sown horticulture crop on the e-Kharid portal during the specified sowing window.
Sell the crop in an official Haryana mandi during the designated sale period and obtain the J-Form.
If the mandi price is lower than the government's base price (e.g., ₹500/quintal for Onion), apply for compensation.
Funds are disbursed within 15 days directly to the bank account.

name: Suryashakti Kisan Yojana (SKY)
ministry: Energy and Petrochemicals Department, Govt of Gujarat
effective_interest_rate_note: The farmer contributes 5% margin money. The State/Center provides a 60% subsidy. The remaining 35% is provided as a low-cost loan at <6% interest for 7 years.
eligibility_human: Farmers in Gujarat connected to the agricultural electricity grid, willing to install solar panels on their land to generate captive power for irrigation and sell surplus power to the DISCOM.
pros: Transforms farmers into power producers. Surplus electricity is bought by the government at ₹7/unit for the first 7 years.
Requires incredibly low upfront investment (only 5% of the total project cost).
cons: Requires dedicating a portion of the agricultural land to mount the PV modules (though elevated mounting is an option).
application_steps: Farmers on a specific agricultural feeder form a committee.
Apply through the local DISCOM subdivision office.
Pay the 5% upfront cost.
Government facilitates the 35% loan and installs the net-metered solar panels.
Revenue from surplus power is used to automatically pay off the 35% loan EMIs over 7 years.

name: Mukhyamantri Matsya Sampada Yojana
ministry: Department of Fisheries, Govt of Uttarakhand

interest_subvention.note: A 5% interest subsidy is provided on bank loans for pond construction (3% state + 2% central PMMSY convergence).

women_sc_st.note: Women, SC, and ST applicants receive up to 60% capital subsidy compared to 50% for general categories.

effective_interest_rate_note: Provides a 5% interest reduction on commercial bank rates alongside a 50-60% capital subsidy for fisheries infrastructure.
eligibility_human: Fish farmers and women groups in Uttarakhand holding own or leased land suitable for pond or raceway construction (hilly/plains).
pros: Tailors PMMSY benefits specifically to hilly terrain, subsidizing raceways and trout farming.
Provides state-sponsored insurance of ₹1 Lakh for fish farmers (90% premium paid by govt).
cons: Subsidy amounts are strictly capped per hectare/cubic meter according to state technical norms.
application_steps: Submit application on the state fisheries portal.
Fisheries inspector surveys the site and prepares a technical proposal.
Beneficiary constructs the pond via self-funding or bank loan.
Subsidy and 5% interest subvention are credited directly to the beneficiary's bank account.

name: Mukhyamantri Saur Krushi Pump Yojana (MSKPY)
ministry: Energy Department, Govt of Maharashtra

sc_st_farmers.note: SC/ST farmers pay only 5% of the pump cost. General category farmers pay 10% (90% subsidy).

effective_interest_rate_note: A massive direct capital subsidy eliminating the need for loan financing. Farmer pays only 5-10% of the pump cost upfront.
eligibility_human: Farmers in Maharashtra possessing agricultural land with an assured water source (well, borewell, river) but DO NOT have a conventional agricultural electricity connection.
pros: Delivers daytime reliable power for irrigation instantly, bypassing the multi-year waiting list for grid electricity.
Extremely low out-of-pocket cost (5-10%).
cons: Farmers who already hold an MSEDCL agricultural power connection are strictly disqualified.
application_steps: Register on the MSEDCL MSKPY portal.
Upload 7/12 extract and Aadhaar details.
Upon document approval, pay the 5% or 10% beneficiary share online.
MSEDCL assigns an empanelled agency to supply and install the 3 HP, 5 HP, or 7.5 HP solar pump.

name: Dr. YSR Free Crop Insurance Scheme
ministry: Agriculture Department, Govt of Andhra Pradesh
effective_interest_rate_note: The state government pays the 100% farmer's share of the premium for the Pradhan Mantri Fasal Bima Yojana (PMFBY).
eligibility_human: All farmers and tenant farmers in Andhra Pradesh who register their cultivated crops on the e-Crop booking portal before the season deadline.
pros: Relieves the farmer entirely from paying crop insurance premiums.
Universal coverage for both loanee and non-loanee farmers through simple e-Crop registration.
cons: Failure to register the exact crop sown on the e-Crop portal during the narrow sowing window voids all coverage.
application_steps: Visit the local Rythu Bharosa Kendra (RBK) during the Kharif/Rabi sowing season.
Complete e-Crop booking with the Village Agriculture Assistant (VAA).
The State Government pays the PMFBY premium on the farmer's behalf.
In case of notified natural calamities or yield loss, the claim amount is credited via DBT to the Aadhaar-linked account.

name: Mukhyamantri Krishi Ashirwad Yojana (MMKAY)
ministry: Agriculture, Animal Husbandry & Co-operative Department
effective_interest_rate_note: A pure direct cash transfer scheme to support agricultural input costs.
eligibility_human: Small and marginal farmers in Jharkhand owning up to 5 acres of cultivable land. Excludes government employees, taxpayers, and urban landholders.
pros: Provides ₹5,000 per acre per year (up to a maximum of 5 acres or ₹25,000) directly to the farmer.
Can be used for any input cost (seeds, fertilizer, labor) regardless of the crop grown.
cons: Strictly limited to a maximum payout of 5 acres; larger farmers are excluded entirely.
application_steps: Apply online on the MMKAY portal or through the local Krishi Prasar Karyalaya.
Submit land ownership documents and Aadhaar.
Revenue authorities verify land records.
Approved applications receive funds directly via DBT each agricultural season.

name: Prakritik Kheti Khushhal Kisan Yojana (PK3Y)
ministry: Agriculture Department, Govt of Himachal Pradesh

desi_cow_purchase.note: Provides 50% subsidy (up to ₹25,000) for purchasing indigenous (Desi) cows essential for natural farming formulations.

effective_interest_rate_note: Direct backend subsidy on the purchase of inputs for natural farming. No loan required.
eligibility_human: Farmers in Himachal Pradesh willing to adopt Subhash Palekar Natural Farming (SPNF) techniques, eliminating chemical fertilizers and pesticides.
pros: Subsidizes 75% of the cost for plastic drums (used to prepare Jeevamrutha) and lining materials.
Provides financial support to buy indigenous cows, which are the backbone of natural farming.
Reduces overall farming costs drastically by eliminating chemical purchases.
cons: Transitioning to natural farming yields can be slow in the first 1-2 years.
application_steps: Register with the local ATMA block officer.
Undergo mandatory training in Subhash Palekar Natural Farming methodologies.
Purchase required materials (drums, cows) and submit bills to ATMA.
Subsidy is credited via DBT to the farmer's account.

name: Mukhya Mantri Krishi Sa-Sajuli Yojna
ministry: Agriculture Department, Govt of Assam
effective_interest_rate_note: A pure direct cash transfer of ₹5,000 intended for farm tools. No loan or repayment involved.
eligibility_human: Small and marginal farmers of Assam (owning more than 1 Bigha but less than 2 Hectares) and active tenant farmers. Minimum age of 21 years.

documents_required.name: Land Patta / Tenant Certification by Gaon Burha

pros: Direct DBT transfer of ₹5,000 gives farmers autonomy to purchase the specific hand-tools or implements they need.
Tenant farmers (who often lack land titles) are eligible with simple certification from the village head.
cons: Only one beneficiary per family is allowed.
A relatively small amount, suitable only for hand tools rather than motorized machinery.
application_steps: Collect application form from the local Agriculture Extension Assistant (AEA).
Submit the filled form along with bank details and land/tenant proof to the AEA.
District Level Committee approves the beneficiary list.
₹5,000 is directly credited to the bank account via DBT.

name: Meghalaya Piggery Mission
ministry: Animal Husbandry & Veterinary Department, Govt of Meghalaya

interest_subvention.note: The state government provides 100% interest subvention. Borrowers repay only the principal amount.

effective_interest_rate_note: 100% interest subvention means the loan is completely interest-free for the borrower, provided EMIs are paid on time.
eligibility_human: Individual farmers, SHGs, and Primary Agricultural Cooperative Societies (PACS) in rural Meghalaya interested in pig breeding and fattening.
pros: 0% interest capital to scale up pig breeding, a highly lucrative market in the North East.
The mission provides high-yield piglets and veterinary support directly.
cons: Borrower must bear the insurance cost of the livestock.
application_steps: Submit application to the local AH & Veterinary Officer.
Officers inspect the proposed site for the pig shed.
Bank sanctions the loan; funds are released directly to empanelled suppliers for piglets and feed.
State government pays the interest component directly to the bank.

name: Mukhyamantri Rubber Mission
ministry: Tribal Welfare Department / Forest Department, Govt of Tripura
effective_interest_rate_note: A 100% financial grant per hectare to establish and maintain rubber plantations over a 5-year gestation period.
eligibility_human: Rural landowners and tribal families in Tripura holding at least 0.5 hectares (approx 1.2 acres) of unutilized or degraded land suitable for rubber plantation.

documents_required.name: Land Patta / Forest Rights Act (FRA) Patta

pros: Fully covers the cost of clearing land, buying rubber stumps, and applying fertilizers for 5 years.
Transforms degraded tribal land into highly lucrative long-term latex-producing assets.
cons: Gestation period is long; rubber trees take 5-7 years before they begin yielding latex/income.
application_steps: Apply through the local TRPC center or Rubber Board field office.
Officials conduct land suitability testing.
Saplings/stumps are provided, and planting is executed.
Maintenance grant is transferred annually to the beneficiary's bank account based on the survival rate of the trees.

name: Mukhyamantri Ghasyari Kalyan Yojana
ministry: Cooperative Department, Govt of Uttarakhand
effective_interest_rate_note: A direct price subsidy. Nutritional cattle feed/fodder is sold to women at ₹2 per kg (heavily subsidized from the market rate).
eligibility_human: Rural women (Ghasyaris) in the hilly districts of Uttarakhand who traditionally spend hours trekking into forests to cut fodder for livestock.
pros: Drastically reduces the physical burden and risk of animal attacks on women collecting forest fodder.
Nutritional silage blocks increase milk yield by 15-20%.
cons: Availability depends strictly on the supply chain efficiency of local PACS.
application_steps: Register at the local Primary Agriculture Credit Society (PACS).
Purchase the 25kg or 30kg vacuum-packed silage blocks at the subsidized rate directly from the cooperative outlet.

name: Telangana State Micro Irrigation Project (TSMIP)
ministry: Agriculture Department, Govt of Telangana

sc_st_farmers.note: 100% free micro-irrigation systems for SC and ST farmers. BC farmers get 90%, and General category farmers get 80% subsidy (up to 5 hectares).

effective_interest_rate_note: Direct capital backend subsidy on the installation invoice.
eligibility_human: Farmers in Telangana owning agricultural land with a viable water source (borewell/open well). Highly subsidized to encourage drip and sprinkler irrigation.
pros: Provides drip/sprinkler systems entirely free (100% subsidy) to SC/ST farmers.
Reduces water consumption by 50% while improving crop yields.
cons: Must purchase the equipment exclusively from government-empanelled MI companies.
application_steps: Apply through the nearest MeeSeva center with land documents and crop details.
Mandal Horticulture Officer conducts a field feasibility survey.
Beneficiary deposits the non-subsidized portion (if applicable) as a DD.
Empanelled vendor installs the system; government pays the vendor the subsidy directly.

name: YSR Rythu Bharosa - PM KISAN
ministry: Agriculture Department, Govt of AP

landless_sc_st_bc.note: Landless tenant farmers and ROFR cultivators belonging to SC, ST, BC, and Minority categories also receive the full ₹13,500 annually (funded entirely by the state, without the PM-KISAN component).

effective_interest_rate_note: A pure direct cash transfer scheme for agricultural investment support.
eligibility_human: All landholding farmer families in AP. Additionally, landless tenant farmers cultivating at least 1 acre (0.5 acres for horticulture) from SC/ST/BC/Minority categories are eligible.

documents_required.name: Crop Cultivation Rights Card (CCRC) for Tenants

pros: Provides ₹13,500 annually (stacked with PM-KISAN) in three installments to meet sowing and harvesting expenses.
One of the few schemes nationally that legally recognizes and funds landless tenant farmers.
cons: Excludes institutional landholders, tax-paying professionals, and government employees.
application_steps: Village volunteers conduct door-to-door surveys to identify cultivators.
Data is cross-verified with Webland and e-Crop portals.
Final eligible lists are displayed at the Grama Sachivalayam.
Funds are released via DBT directly to the Aadhaar-linked bank account.

name: Krushak Assistance for Livelihood and Income Augmentation (KALIA)
ministry: Department of Agriculture and Farmers' Empowerment, Govt of Odisha

landless_households.note: Landless agricultural households receive a one-time grant of ₹12,500 to start allied activities like goat rearing, poultry, or mushroom cultivation. Vulnerable/Elderly landless get ₹10,000/year sustenance.

effective_interest_rate_note: A pure direct cash transfer. Small/Marginal farmers receive ₹4,000 annually (converged with PM-KISAN).
eligibility_human: Small/marginal farmers, landless agricultural laborers, and vulnerable farm families in Odisha. Must not be income tax payers or government employees.
pros: Incredibly inclusive: provides heavy upfront capital (₹12,500) specifically to the landless poor who cannot normally access farm loans.
Includes a robust life insurance (₹2 Lakh) and accident insurance component.
cons: The ongoing annual input assistance for farmers was reduced from ₹10,000 to ₹4,000 to converge with PM-KISAN.
application_steps: Submit the 'Green Form' at the Gram Panchayat office during application phases.
Nodal officers conduct ground verification and cross-check with databases.
Approved lists are finalized and funds transferred directly via DBT.

name: Mukhyamantri Janjati Jeevika Mission (MJJM)
ministry: ST & SC Development, Minorities & Backward Classes Welfare Department
implementing_agency: Tribal Development Cooperative Corporation of Odisha (TDCCOL)
effective_interest_rate_note: A 100% financial grant to improve tribal livelihoods. No loan is required.
eligibility_human: Scheduled Tribe (ST) households residing in the 119 Tribal Sub-Plan (TSP) blocks of Odisha. Focuses on promoting agro-forestry, minor forest produce processing, and livestock rearing.
pros: Provides end-to-end support: from free saplings and goats to setting up processing machinery for Sal leaves/tamarind.
Protects tribal communities from middlemen by funding collective storage and processing infrastructure.
cons: Strictly limited to designated tribal blocks (TSP areas) in the state.
application_steps: Local ITDA officials and NGOs conduct micro-planning at the village level.
Beneficiaries are grouped into producer groups or individual clusters.
Assets (livestock, seeds, processing tools) and capacity building are delivered directly to the village.

name: Bihan (Chhattisgarh State Rural Livelihoods Mission)
ministry: Panchayat and Rural Development Department, Govt of Chhattisgarh

revolving_fund.note: A pure grant of ₹15,000 (Revolving Fund) and up to ₹60,000 (Community Investment Fund) is provided directly to the SHG.

effective_interest_rate_note: Through bank linkages and state interest subvention, SHGs can borrow at incredibly low rates (effective 3% or lower for prompt repayment).
eligibility_human: Rural women in Chhattisgarh organized into Self Help Groups (SHGs) under the Bihan network, having completed 3 to 6 months of regular savings and meetings.
pros: Provides initial non-repayable seed capital to build the group's financial foundation.
Facilitates highly subsidized large-ticket bank loans (Cash Credit limits) without collateral.
cons: Individuals cannot apply; funds must be routed through the collective SHG structure.
application_steps: Women form a 10-15 member group with the help of Community Resource Persons (CRPs).
After 3 months of internal saving, the group receives a ₹15,000 Revolving Fund grant.
After grading, the group prepares a Micro Credit Plan and is linked to a bank for term loans/cash credit.

contact_info.helpline: Contact Local Bihan Block Mission Manager

name: Mukhyamantri Gopalak Yojana
ministry: Animal Husbandry Department, Govt of UP
effective_interest_rate_note: A commercial term loan up to ₹9 Lakh is subsidized by a margin money grant of ₹10,000 per animal (up to ₹90,000) deposited directly by the state over 5 years.
eligibility_human: Unemployed youth in Uttar Pradesh with an annual family income below ₹1 Lakh, looking to set up a dairy unit of 10-20 cows/buffaloes. Must own or lease land for a cattle shed.
pros: Reduces initial capital barrier for setting up mid-scale dairy farms.
The cattle are purchased from state-organized cattle fairs, ensuring quality breeds.
cons: The subsidy is not upfront; it is released in installments of ₹18,000 per year directly to the bank account.
Strict income threshold of ₹1 Lakh restricts many applicants.
application_steps: Submit application to the nearest veterinary hospital or CVO.
District level committee reviews and forwards to a commercial bank.
Bank sanctions the ₹9 Lakh loan.
Applicant purchases 10 animals in Phase 1 and 10 in Phase 2; state releases annual margin money.

name: Mukhyamantri Pashudhan Vikas Yojana
ministry: Animal Husbandry and Dairying Department, MP

sc_st_women.note: SC, ST, and Women beneficiaries receive an enhanced 75% subsidy for establishing poultry, goat, and pig rearing units.

effective_interest_rate_note: A direct capital grant applied to the unit cost of establishing livestock farms. No mandatory bank loan required if self-funded.
eligibility_human: Residents of Madhya Pradesh wishing to start small livestock units (Goat rearing - 10+1 unit, Poultry - Kadaknath/Backyard, Piggery).
pros: Massive 75% subsidy for marginalized groups makes entering livestock rearing virtually risk-free.
Specifically promotes the indigenous and highly profitable 'Kadaknath' poultry breed.
cons: Stock availability depends on state-run hatcheries and breeding farms, which may cause delays.
application_steps: Submit application to the local veterinary surgeon or Deputy Director's office.
Deposit the beneficiary share (25% or 50% via DD).
Department supplies the livestock unit (animals, initial feed, and vaccines) directly.

name: Mukhyamantri Kisan Mitra Urja Yojana
ministry: Energy Department, Govt of Rajasthan
effective_interest_rate_note: A direct tariff subsidy applied to the agricultural electricity bill. No loan involved.
eligibility_human: Metered agricultural power consumers (farmers) in Rajasthan. Employees of central/state governments and income taxpayers are strictly excluded.
pros: Provides a flat subsidy of ₹1,000 per month (₹12,000 annually) directly adjusting the electricity bill, effectively making electricity free for small farmers.
cons: Subsidy is only credited if there are no previous outstanding power dues on the meter.
application_steps: Link Aadhaar and bank account to the DISCOM agricultural connection.
Clear any outstanding historical power dues.
The DISCOM automatically deducts ₹1,000 from the bi-monthly generated bill. Any surplus subsidy is adjusted in the next billing cycle.

name: Pashu Bhagya Scheme
ministry: Department of Animal Husbandry and Fisheries, Govt of Karnataka

sc_st_beneficiaries.note: SC and ST beneficiaries receive an enhanced 70% back-ended capital subsidy up to ₹2.24 Lakh.

effective_interest_rate_note: Short-term livestock loans up to ₹50,000 carry a 0% interest rate. For larger livestock term loans, the state provides interest subvention capping the effective borrowing rate at nominal levels.
eligibility_human: Small and marginal farmers, agricultural laborers, and rural women in Karnataka establishing dairy units (2 cows/buffaloes), sheep/goat rearing (10+1 or 20+1 units), piggery, or backyard poultry.

documents_required.name: Land Records or Gram Panchayat Shelter Clearance

pros: Subsidizes up to 70% of livestock unit costs for SC/ST farmers and 50% for others.
Includes a 0% interest window for short-term working capital up to ₹50,000.
Comprehensive insurance cover for animals with subsidized premiums.
cons: Beneficiary selection is quota-based and allocated across Assembly constituencies.
application_steps: Obtain and submit the application at the local Government Veterinary Hospital.
Taluk Level Selection Committee shortlists applicants and sponsors files to banks.
Bank disburses the loan component.
Department releases the back-ended subsidy and assists in purchasing tagged livestock.

name: Swavalambi Sarathi Scheme
ministry: Social Welfare / Backward Classes Welfare Department, Govt of Karnataka
implementing_agency: State Development Corporations (Dr. B.R. Ambedkar, D. Devaraj Urs, KMDC)

sc_st_youth.note: Under the SC/ST Development Corporation, the capital subsidy on commercial vehicle purchases is enhanced up to 75% or ₹3.5 Lakh.

effective_interest_rate_note: Standard commercial vehicle financing rates apply. The government provides 50% to 75% margin money subsidy, significantly lowering loan principal.
eligibility_human: Unemployed youth in Karnataka belonging to SC, ST, Backward Classes, or Minority communities aged 21-45 who hold a valid commercial driving license, purchasing a commercial four-wheeler (goods auto, pickup truck, taxi).
pros: Provides ₹3 Lakh to ₹3.5 Lakh as a non-repayable grant to acquire a commercial freight vehicle.
Eliminates heavy personal down payments, allowing drivers to become vehicle owners.
cons: The beneficiary cannot sell or transfer the vehicle for a mandatory lock-in period of 5 years.
application_steps: Apply online via Seva Sindhu or Grama One center.
District screening committee verifies caste, income, and driving credentials.
Applicant is linked to a participating bank for the remaining balance.
Subsidy is credited directly to the vehicle dealer to deliver the on-road vehicle.

name: Badavara Bandhu Scheme
ministry: Cooperation Department, Govt of Karnataka
implementing_agency: District Central Cooperative Banks (DCCBs) / Town Cooperative Banks
effective_interest_rate_note: Completely 0% interest. Micro-loans up to ₹10,000 are provided interest-free and collateral-free. The state government compensates cooperative banks for operational costs.
eligibility_human: Small roadside vendors, vegetable/fruit sellers, flower merchants, and mobile push-cart operators in rural, semi-urban, and urban market yards across Karnataka.

documents_required.name: Street Vending Identity Card / Letter from Local Body

pros: Eliminates reliance on exploitative private moneylenders (who charge daily compound rates).
Flexible daily/weekly repayment schedule (e.g., ₹100 per day) without any interest charge.
Successful repayment instantly renews the credit limit.
cons: Short repayment window (typically 90 days).
Ticket size is strictly capped at ₹10,000.
application_steps: Approach the local DCC Bank or mobile cooperative van stationed at the market yard.
Submit Aadhaar and vendor proof.
Receive cash or direct bank transfer on the same day.
Deposit daily earnings into the bank counter or with the visiting recovery agent.

name: Bhausaheb Fundkar Shetkari Phalbag Lagwad Yojana
ministry: Agriculture & Horticulture Department, Govt of Maharashtra
effective_interest_rate_note: A 100% financial assistance grant disbursed over 3 years: 50% in Year 1, 30% in Year 2, and 20% in Year 3 based on plant survival rates.
eligibility_human: Farmers in Maharashtra owning between 0.20 hectares (0.5 acres) and 6 hectares of land with an assured water source, establishing permanent orchards of 16 notified fruit crops (Mango, Pomegranate, Guava, Custard Apple, Orange, Sweet Lime, Cashew, etc.).
pros: 100% cost coverage covering pit digging, saplings, bio-fertilizers, fencing, and drip integration.
Guarantees 3 consecutive years of financial support to ensure saplings survive until commercial fruiting.
cons: Second and third-year grants require a strict minimum survival rate (75% for dryland trees, 90% for irrigated trees).
application_steps: Register and apply under 'Horticulture Schemes' on the MahaDBT farmer portal.
Receive online pre-sanction letter after electronic draw.
Procure certified saplings from government-accredited nurseries and execute plantation.
Taluka agriculture officer conducts geo-tagged inspection; subsidy tranches are released via DBT.

name: Sant Rohidas Charmakar Special Subsidy & Margin Scheme
ministry: Social Justice and Special Assistance Department, Govt of Maharashtra
implementing_agency: Sant Rohidas Leather Industries & Charmakar Development Corporation (LIDCOM)

term_loan_tier.note: For project costs between ₹1 Lakh and ₹5 Lakh, LIDCOM provides 20% margin money at 4% interest, bank finances 75%, and applicant contributes only 5%.

effective_interest_rate_note: On the small loan tier (up to ₹50,000), 100% of the loan is provided as an upfront capital subsidy (₹25,000) and an interest-free balance.
eligibility_human: Artisans belonging to the Charmakar (Leather/Cobbler) community in Maharashtra aged 18-50 with annual family income below ₹1 Lakh, undertaking footwear, leathercraft, or retail ventures.
pros: Direct 50% non-repayable capital subsidy on small equipment/raw material purchases.
Extremely cheap 4% soft loans to protect traditional leather workers from high-interest suppliers.
cons: Strict sub-caste verification required.
application_steps: Collect form from the District Manager, LIDCOM office.
Attach caste, income, and project proposal for footwear/leather retail.
LIDCOM District Committee approves and forwards to a commercial bank.
Subsidy is released directly to the supplier/bank account.

name: YSR Matsyakara Bharosa
ministry: Fisheries Department, Govt of Andhra Pradesh

fuel_subsidy.note: Provides ₹9 per liter diesel subsidy for motorized boats (up to 300 liters/month) and mechanized boats (up to 3,000 liters/month).

effective_interest_rate_note: A pure direct cash grant of ₹10,000 transferred during the annual marine fishing ban period (April 15 to June 14). No loan involved.
eligibility_human: Marine fisher families operating motorized, mechanized, or traditional non-motorized boats in coastal districts of Andhra Pradesh impacted by the annual sea-fishing ban.
pros: Provides critical subsistence income (₹10,000) during the 61-day fishing ban.
The enhanced ₹9/liter diesel subsidy drastically cuts operational running costs for deep-sea fishers.
cons: All boat crew members must be registered and verified via biometric muster rolls; unregistered helpers are excluded.
application_steps: Village Fisheries Assistant conducts annual enumeration of active fishermen and boats at the landing center.
Social audit list displayed at local Grama Sachivalayam.
Funds transferred via DBT to the head of the fisher family during the ban period.

name: YSR Jagananna Thodu
ministry: Finance / Village & Ward Secretariats, Govt of AP

step_up_credit.note: Successful repayment of the first ₹10,000 cycle unlocks enhanced interest-free limits of ₹12,000 and ₹15,000 in subsequent cycles.

effective_interest_rate_note: 100% interest subvention. Borrowers repay bank installments, and the state deposits the full interest amount directly back into their bank accounts every 6 months.
eligibility_human: Small street vendors, vegetable sellers, fruit pushcart owners, potters, weavers, and tiny grocery store operators in rural and urban Andhra Pradesh. Family income must be under ₹10,000/month (rural) or ₹12,000/month (urban).
pros: Collateral-free working capital of ₹10,000 entirely free of interest.
Automated interest subvention credited twice a year without requiring the vendor to visit bank branches.
cons: Late payment of monthly installments delays or forfeits the interest refund.
application_steps: Village volunteer maps the street vendor using the GSWS mobile app.
Welfare assistant verifies the stall/cart location.
Bank disburses ₹10,000 loan without collateral.
Vendor pays monthly EMIs; government reimburses the interest directly.

name: Telangana Chenetha Mitra Scheme
ministry: Handlooms and Textiles Department, Govt of Telangana
effective_interest_rate_note: A direct 40% input subsidy credited via DBT on purchases of yarn, dyes, and chemicals.
eligibility_human: Individual handloom weavers, ancillary workers, and master weavers in Telangana who produce handloom cloth and purchase raw materials from authorized yarn depots (NHDC or cooperative depots).

documents_required.name: Purchase Invoices for Yarn and Dyes

pros: Direct 40% cash back on yarn and chemical costs significantly boosts the operating profit margins of rural weavers.
Capped at ₹3,000 per loom per month (up to ₹36,000 per year).
cons: Purchases must be made strictly from government-empanelled yarn depots or cooperative bodies.
application_steps: Ensure the handloom is geo-tagged and registered with the district handloom office.
Purchase raw materials from an approved yarn dealer and submit invoices online.
Department verifies procurement volume against weaving capacity.
40% subsidy is deposited directly into the weaver's bank account.

name: TABCEDCO Micro Credit & Term Loan Scheme
ministry: Backward Classes, Most Backward Classes and Minorities Welfare Department
implementing_agency: Tamil Nadu Backward Classes Economic Development Corporation (TABCEDCO)

women_shg_rebate.note: Women Self Help Groups receive micro-credit up to ₹1.25 Lakh per member at a heavily discounted interest rate of 4% per annum.

effective_interest_rate_note: Term loans charged at 6% to 8% per annum (significantly lower than commercial lending rates). Micro-finance for SHG women provided at only 4% per annum.
eligibility_human: Individuals belonging to Backward Classes (BC), Most Backward Classes (MBC), and Denotified Communities (DNC) in Tamil Nadu with annual family income up to ₹3 Lakh, establishing small trade, service, or agro-ventures.
pros: 4% flat interest rate for rural women SHGs allows affordable scaling of village cottage ventures.
High loan limits up to ₹15 Lakh for individual business expansion without private moneylenders.
cons: Requires processing through cooperative bank channels, which may require local asset hypothecation or guarantors.
application_steps: Obtain application form from District Backward Classes and Minorities Welfare Office or local DCCB branch.
Submit completed form with project report and caste credentials.
DCCB appraises credit viability and disburses subsidized funds.

name: Free Milch Cows and Sheep/Goats Distribution Scheme
ministry: Animal Husbandry, Dairying and Fisheries Department, Govt of Tamil Nadu
effective_interest_rate_note: A 100% free government grant. Female beneficiaries are given 1 milch cow or 4 sheep/goats completely free of cost along with free transit insurance.
eligibility_human: Poorest-of-the-poor landless rural women in Tamil Nadu (widows, destitute, deserted women, and transgender women given priority). Applicant must not own any existing cattle or land.
pros: Transfers an income-generating asset at zero debt liability.
Includes free feed for the initial weeks and free livestock insurance coverage for 3 years.
Guarantees daily income through local Aavin milk cooperative procurement.
cons: Strict prohibition against selling the allotted livestock; regular spot inspections are conducted.
application_steps: Beneficiary list is drawn up and finalized at the local Gram Sabha meeting.
Veterinary department verifies applicant's landless status with the VAO.
Beneficiary accompanies veterinary officials to cattle shandies to select the cow/goats.
Livestock is ear-tagged and handed over with free insurance documents.

name: Scheme for Maintenance of Indigenous (Desi) Cow in Organic Farming
ministry: Agriculture, Farmers Welfare and Cooperation Department, Govt of Gujarat
effective_interest_rate_note: A monthly cash transfer of ₹900 (totaling ₹10,800 per year) directly to the farmer's bank account. No loan involved.
eligibility_human: Farmers in Gujarat practicing certified natural/organic farming on their land and maintaining at least one tagged indigenous Desi cow.
pros: Covers the ongoing maintenance and fodder cost of maintaining a Desi cow used for preparing Jeevamrutha.
Completely digital application and verification via the iKhedut portal.
cons: Limited to only one cow per farmer family.
Requires active enrollment in natural farming programs.
application_steps: Register the tagged indigenous cow with the local veterinary officer.
Apply online on the iKhedut portal under 'Animal Husbandry Schemes'.
Upload land records and natural farming declaration.
₹900/month is credited quarterly directly into the farmer's bank account.

name: Kisan Parivahan Yojana
ministry: Agriculture, Farmers Welfare and Cooperation Department, Govt of Gujarat

sc_st_small_farmers.note: Small, Marginal, SC, and ST farmers receive 50% capital subsidy up to ₹75,000. General category receives 35% up to ₹50,000.

effective_interest_rate_note: A direct capital grant reducing the purchase cost of a small cargo/utility vehicle to transport agricultural produce.
eligibility_human: Farmers holding agricultural land in Gujarat purchasing small utility goods vehicles (e.g., Tata Ace, Mahindra Bolero Maxi Truck) to transport crops directly to agricultural markets.
pros: Enables farmers to bypass middle-tier transport cartels and bring produce directly to urban APMC markets.
Up to ₹75,000 upfront subsidy directly credited against vehicle invoice.
cons: Vehicle must be registered strictly as an agricultural/commercial transport vehicle under the farmer's name.
application_steps: Apply online on the iKhedut portal when the application window opens.
Obtain in-principle sanction order from the District Agriculture Officer.
Purchase the vehicle from an authorized dealer within 30 days.
Upload RC book, chassis number, and insurance; subsidy is credited to the bank account.

name: Acharya Vidyasagar Gau Samvardhan Yojana
ministry: Animal Husbandry and Dairying Department, Govt of MP

sc_st_farmers.note: SC and ST farmers receive 75% subsidy (up to ₹2 Lakh) on a project of 5 or more cattle. General category gets 50% subsidy (up to ₹1.5 Lakh).

effective_interest_rate_note: Standard bank term loan rates apply. The government provides 50% to 75% back-ended capital subsidy to clear the loan principal.
eligibility_human: Farmers in Madhya Pradesh owning at least 1 acre of agricultural land for growing green fodder, establishing small dairy farms of minimum 5 milch cattle (cows or buffaloes).
pros: Supports establishment of commercially viable 5-animal micro-dairies with up to 75% subsidy.
Integrated with MP State Cooperative Dairy Federation (Sanchi) for assured daily milk collection.
cons: Applicant must officially dedicate 1 acre of land strictly to cultivating green fodder.
application_steps: Submit application at the local veterinary hospital.
Veterinary officer inspects the fodder land and cattle shed.
Application is forwarded to a commercial bank branch for term loan sanction.
Cattle purchased from state fairs; subsidy held as TDR and adjusted against the loan.

contact_info.helpline: Contact Local Deputy Director Veterinary Services

name: Uttar Pradesh Kukkut Vikas Niti (Commercial Poultry Policy)
ministry: Animal Husbandry Department, Govt of Uttar Pradesh
implementing_agency: Directorate of Animal Husbandry / Commercial Banks

interest_subvention.note: State government pays 100% of the bank loan interest (up to 7% or 10% benchmark) for a full period of 5 years on loans up to ₹1.6 Crore.

effective_interest_rate_note: A 100% interest subvention scheme on commercial bank loans for 5 years. Borrower repays only the principal loan amount.
eligibility_human: Rural entrepreneurs and farmers in Uttar Pradesh establishing commercial broiler (10,000 birds) or commercial layer units (30,000 to 60,000 birds). Must hold unencumbered land for poultry sheds.

documents_required.name: Land Title Deed (Minimum 1 to 3 acres unencumbered)
Detailed Project Report (DPR) approved by Bank

pros: Enables large-scale agro-industrial units with interest payments completely covered by the state for 5 years.
Includes 100% stamp duty exemption on purchasing or leasing agricultural land for poultry farms.
cons: Requires substantial promoter equity (minimum 15% to 20% of project cost) and large land tracts.
application_steps: Submit poultry project proposal to the District Chief Veterinary Officer.
District Level Committee scrutinizes land suitability and bio-security parameters.
Proposal is sponsored to a commercial bank for term loan sanction.
Animal Husbandry Department deposits interest subvention directly to the bank account annually.

name: Pandit Deendayal Gramodyog Rojgar Yojana
ministry: MSME and Export Promotion Department, Govt of UP

women_sc_st.note: 100% interest subvention for 3 years for SC, ST, OBC, Women, and Minorities. General category pays a fixed subsidized interest rate.

effective_interest_rate_note: A 100% interest subsidy on bank term loans up to ₹25 Lakh for the first 3 years, making debt completely interest-free for rural entrepreneurs.
eligibility_human: Unemployed rural youth of Uttar Pradesh aged 18 to 50 setting up cottage, village, or agro-processing manufacturing enterprises in Gram Panchayat areas.

documents_required.name: UP Domicile & Gram Panchayat Rural Residence Proof

pros: Provides up to ₹25 Lakh in capital completely interest-free for the initial critical 3 years.
Directly promotes rural industrialization, stopping urban distress migration.
cons: Enterprise must be located strictly outside urban municipal limits.
application_steps: Submit application online via the UPKVIB portal.
District Task Force Committee evaluates business viability.
Application is forwarded to the bank branch for CGTMSE-backed loan sanction.
UPKVIB credits the interest reimbursement amount directly to the bank account quarterly.

contact_info.helpline: Contact Local District Village Industries Office

name: Punjab Dairy Development Commercial Subsidy Scheme
ministry: Animal Husbandry, Fisheries & Dairy Development, Govt of Punjab

sc_beneficiaries.note: SC category dairy farmers receive a 33% capital subsidy (up to ₹2.31 Lakh) on establishing a 10-milch cattle dairy unit.

effective_interest_rate_note: Direct capital backend subsidy on automated milking machines, cattle sheds, and milch cow purchases.
eligibility_human: Farmers and rural youth in Punjab aged 18-55 establishing dairy units of 2 to 20 crossbred cows/buffaloes, possessing certified 2-4 week dairy training from PDDB training centers.
pros: Extensive financial coverage: subsidizes cattle purchase, modern cattle sheds, milking parlors, and silage bale wrapping machines.
Integrates with the Verka cooperative network for assured off-take of milk.
cons: Mandatory completion of the PDDB residential training course prior to application.
application_steps: Complete 2-week Dairy Entrepreneurship Training at nearest PDDB training center.
Submit application with bank sanction to the Deputy Director Dairy.
Purchase certified high-yield cattle.
Inspection committee verifies cattle tags and sheds; subsidy is released to the bank.

name: Gatidhara Scheme
ministry: Transport Department, Govt of West Bengal

women_and_sc_st.note: Special category and female beneficiaries receive expedited sponsorship and task force priority.

effective_interest_rate_note: Standard commercial vehicle bank lending rates apply. The State Government provides a 30% margin money subsidy (capped at ₹1 Lakh) to bridge the down payment.
eligibility_human: Unemployed youth of West Bengal aged 20-45 registered in the Employment Bank with annual family income up to ₹3 Lakh, buying a commercial small goods vehicle, auto, or passenger taxi.
pros: Provides up to ₹1 Lakh free down payment grant, allowing youth in rural areas to enter the logistics/taxi sector.
Permits purchase of small cargo loaders crucial for moving agricultural goods to wholesale mandis.
cons: Only one person per family can avail of the benefit.
Must have an active commercial driving license at the time of application.
application_steps: Submit application form at the local RTO office, BDO office, or during Duare Sarkar camps.
District Screening Committee interviews applicant and approves vehicle choice.
Offer letter issued; applicant approaches participating bank for loan.
State transfers ₹1 Lakh directly to the vehicle dealership as the down payment.

name: Assam Muga & Eri Silk Mission
ministry: Handloom, Textiles & Sericulture Department, Govt of Assam
effective_interest_rate_note: A 100% free capital and input grant. Rearing houses and cocoon processing kits are provided without any financial loan.
eligibility_human: Rural families, traditional sericulture farmers, and women self-help groups in Assam holding at least 0.5 acres of land planted with host food plants (Som/Soalu for Muga or Kesseru for Eri).

documents_required.name: Land Records / Patta of Host Plantation

pros: Protects and commercializes the globally unique Golden Muga silk.
Provides complete grant funding up to ₹1.25 Lakh to build a scientific silkworm rearing house and supplies disease-free layings (DFLs) free of cost.
cons: Strict requirement of having established host food tree plantations.
application_steps: Apply through the local Sericulture Demonstrator or District Sericulture Officer.
Inspection of host plant plantation on the farmer's land.
Approved beneficiaries receive construction grants in installments and modern rearing equipment kits.
Cocoon buy-back is guaranteed via government reeling units.

name: Mission for Integrated Development of Horticulture (MIDH)
ministry: Ministry of Agriculture & Farmers Welfare

scheduled_hilly_areas.note: Subsidy jumps to 55% for North Eastern Region (NER), Himalayan States, and scheduled areas.

effective_interest_rate_note: A direct capital subsidy calculated on the normative cost of the project (e.g., polyhouses, cold storages, pack houses).
eligibility_human: Farmers, Farmer Producer Organizations (FPOs), SHGs, Cooperatives, and private entrepreneurs setting up horticulture infrastructure like green houses, cold storages, ripening chambers, and high-tech nurseries.
pros: Substantial capital subsidy (40% to 55%) for setting up high-value cold chain and post-harvest infrastructure.
Can be converged seamlessly with the Agriculture Infrastructure Fund (AIF) for additional 3% interest subvention.
cons: Requires heavy upfront capital; the subsidy is strictly back-ended and disbursed only after project completion.
application_steps: Submit DPR to the State Horticulture Mission or National Horticulture Board.
Obtain Letter of Intent (LOI) / In-principle approval.
Secure term loan and execute the physical construction of the facility.
Joint Inspection Team (JIT) evaluates the completed project and releases the backend subsidy to the loan account.

name: Venture Capital Fund for Scheduled Castes (VCF-SC)
ministry: Ministry of Social Justice & Empowerment

women_pwd_concession.note: Companies promoted by SC Women or SC Disabled entrepreneurs receive an additional 0.25% concession on the base interest rate (if structured as debt).

effective_interest_rate_note: Financial assistance is provided as equity, optionally convertible preference shares, or debentures. If structured as debt, the interest rate is highly concessional (typically around 8% p.a. linked to cost of funds).
eligibility_human: Private Limited or Public Limited Companies where Scheduled Caste (SC) entrepreneurs hold at least 51% of the shareholding and management control. Not applicable for proprietorships or LLPs.
pros: Provides massive institutional venture capital (up to ₹15 Crore) to SC entrepreneurs, which is exceptionally rare.
Flexible structuring: funds can be injected as equity or concessional debt with up to a 3-year moratorium.
cons: Strict corporate governance requirements; only formally incorporated Companies (Pvt/Public Ltd) can apply.
Complex and rigorous venture due diligence process by IFCI.
application_steps: Submit preliminary application and pitch deck online on the VCF-SC portal.
Undergo initial screening by IFCI Venture investment committee.
Complete extensive financial, legal, and technical due diligence.
Sign Term Sheet and execute investment agreements for fund disbursement.

name: Fisheries and Aquaculture Infrastructure Development Fund (FIDF)
ministry: Ministry of Fisheries, Animal Husbandry & Dairying
effective_interest_rate_note: Provides a massive 3% interest subvention per annum, capping the maximum lending rate charged to the beneficiary at 9% (and often lower).
eligibility_human: Private entrepreneurs, FPOs, Cooperatives, and State Governments undertaking large fisheries infrastructure projects (e.g., fishing harbours, fish processing plants, ice plants, deep-sea vessels).
pros: Significantly de-risks large marine and aquaculture infrastructure investments via 3% continuous interest subvention.
Extremely long repayment tenure (up to 12 years including 2 years moratorium).
cons: Borrower must bear at least a 20% margin money contribution (own equity).
Approval process requires central committee clearance (CAC) for large projects.
application_steps: Prepare a comprehensive DPR aligned with FIDF guidelines.
Submit application through the FIDF online portal to NFDB.
Central Approval Committee (CAC) appraises and recommends the project.
Nodal Lending Entity (Bank/NABARD) disburses the loan and claims the 3% interest subvention annually.

name: Dairy Processing and Infrastructure Development Fund (DIDF)
ministry: Department of Animal Husbandry & Dairying (DAHD)
effective_interest_rate_note: A highly concessional loan. DAHD provides an interest subvention of 2.5% to NABARD, ensuring the end borrower (Milk Cooperatives/FPOs) receives the loan at an effective rate of around 6% to 6.5% p.a.
eligibility_human: Milk Producer Companies, Farmer Producer Organizations (FPOs), and State Dairy Cooperative Federations looking to establish or modernize milk processing plants, chilling centers, and bulk milk coolers.
pros: Provides massive, ultra-cheap capital (up to 80% of project cost) to build state-of-the-art dairy processing infrastructure.
Excellent 10-year repayment window with a 2-year moratorium on principal.
cons: Private individual entrepreneurs (proprietorships) are strictly excluded; must be a cooperative, FPO, or state federation.
application_steps: Eligible entity prepares a DPR and submits it to NDDB or NCDC.
NDDB evaluates technical and financial viability.
NABARD releases funds to NDDB, which then disburses the concessional loan to the end borrower.
State government steps in as a guarantor for certain cooperative federation loans.

name: ODOP Training and Toolkit Scheme
ministry: Department of MSME & Export Promotion, Govt of UP
effective_interest_rate_note: A 100% free capacity building grant. Participants receive 10 days of free residential training, a daily stipend (₹200/day), and an advanced toolkit related to their district's ODOP craft upon completion.
eligibility_human: Artisans, weavers, and craftsmen in Uttar Pradesh aged 18+ engaged in the specific craft/trade identified as their district's 'One District One Product' (e.g., Chikankari in Lucknow, Carpet weaving in Bhadohi). No educational qualification needed.
pros: Provides high-quality, modern, free toolkits to upgrade traditional crafting methods.
Pays a stipend during the 10-day training to compensate for lost daily wages.
cons: Applicants are strictly restricted to the specific product mapped to their home district.
application_steps: Apply online on the DIUPMSME portal under the ODOP Training Scheme.
DIC verification committee selects candidates.
Attend the 10-day skill upgradation training.
Receive the free toolkit and stipend on the final day.

name: Mukhyamantri Seekho Kamao Yojana (MMSKY)
ministry: Skill Development and Employment Department, MP

education_tier.note: Stipend scales with education: 12th pass gets ₹8,000/month, ITI gets ₹8,500/month, Diploma gets ₹9,000/month, and Graduates get ₹10,000/month for a 1-year training period.

effective_interest_rate_note: A 100% direct stipend transfer to youth acting as on-the-job trainees (apprentices) in private enterprises.
eligibility_human: Unemployed youth of Madhya Pradesh aged 18 to 29 who possess at least a 12th standard pass or ITI certification, looking for on-the-job training in private companies.

documents_required.name: Aadhaar Card linked to DBT bank account

pros: Provides immediate financial independence (₹8,000 to ₹10,000 per month) while learning practical industry skills.
The state government bears 75% of the stipend cost directly via DBT, making it highly attractive for private companies to hire trainees.
cons: Requires matching with an empanelled private establishment; trainees cannot claim the stipend independently.
application_steps: Youth registers on the MMSKY portal using Samagra ID.
Creates a resume and applies for vacancies posted by registered companies.
Company conducts an interview and selects the candidate.
Candidate undergoes 1-year training; state transfers 75% of the stipend directly via DBT, and the company pays 25%.

name: Vazhndhu Kattuvom Project (TNRTP)
ministry: Rural Development and Panchayat Raj Department, Govt of TN

youth_and_women_collectives.note: A Matching Grant up to 30% of the bank loan is given to individual enterprises (max ₹1.5 Lakh) and collective enterprises/FPOs (max ₹4 Lakh).

effective_interest_rate_note: A direct Matching Grant Programme (MGP) that reduces the principal bank loan obligation by 30% for rural enterprises.
eligibility_human: Rural entrepreneurs, SHG members, and FPOs in designated TNRTP blocks of Tamil Nadu undertaking non-farm enterprises or agri-allied value addition.
pros: World Bank-supported project providing robust matching grants to incentivize formal bank credit for rural businesses.
Strong emphasis on capacity building, offering extensive business plan drafting support via Community Professionals.
cons: Restricted exclusively to specific targeted rural blocks in Tamil Nadu; urban enterprises are entirely excluded.
application_steps: Draft a business plan with the help of a TNRTP Enterprise Community Professional (ECP).
Get the plan vetted by the local Village Poverty Reduction Committee (VPRC).
Approach a participating bank for loan sanction.
Upon loan disbursement, TNRTP transfers the 30% matching grant to the loan account.

name: Odisha Youth Innovation Fund
ministry: MSME Department, Govt of Odisha
implementing_agency: Odisha Small Industries Corporation (OSIC) / Startup Odisha

stage_based_grants.note: ₹50,000 for a new validated idea; ₹3 Lakhs for developing a working prototype; and ₹5 Lakhs for registering an enterprise based on the prototype.

effective_interest_rate_note: A 100% non-repayable grant to foster grass-roots innovation.
eligibility_human: Youth of Odisha aged 13 to 35 (includes students, dropouts, and young professionals) who have conceptualized a novel technological, social, or process innovation.

documents_required.name: Proof of Age and Odisha Residence
Detailed Innovation Pitch / Prototype Demo Video

pros: Extremely low barrier to entry—even teenagers (13+) can apply and win ₹50,000 just for a validated idea.
Provides structured scaling: if the idea works, the state grants an additional ₹3 Lakhs to build the physical prototype.
cons: Requires rigorous technical evaluation by a screening committee; standard retail or trading ideas are instantly rejected.
application_steps: Submit the innovative idea or prototype design on the Startup Odisha portal.
The preliminary screening committee evaluates the submission for novelty and commercial viability.
Applicant pitches to the Selection Committee.
Grant is transferred via DBT to fuel prototype development.

name: Gujarat Industrial Policy - Capital Subsidy for MSMEs
ministry: Industries and Mines Department, Govt of Gujarat

taluka_categories.note: Category 1 (Backward Talukas): 25% subsidy up to ₹35 Lakh. Category 2: 20% up to ₹30 Lakh. Category 3: 10% up to ₹10 Lakh. Interest subvention is 7%, 6%, and 5% respectively.

effective_interest_rate_note: A highly attractive 5% to 7% interest subvention for 7 years on term loans, combined with an upfront Fixed Capital Investment (FCI) capital subsidy.
eligibility_human: Manufacturing MSMEs establishing new greenfield units or undertaking substantial expansion in Gujarat.

documents_required.name: Bank Term Loan Sanction and Disbursal Letter

pros: One of the most aggressive industrial MSME policies in India, combining up to ₹35 Lakh capital subsidy with 7 years of 7% interest subvention.
100% reimbursement of EPF contribution for female employees.
cons: Highly complex compliance and auditing required to claim post-production reimbursements.
Trading, retail, and standalone logistics are generally excluded.
application_steps: Register the intent to invest on the Investor Facilitation Portal (IFP).
Construct the plant, install machinery, and begin commercial production.
File claims for capital and interest subsidies online with CA certificates.
State Level Committee approves and processes the annual reimbursement.

name: WE Mission Kerala (Women Entrepreneurship)
ministry: Industries Department, Govt of Kerala

interest_tiers.note: Loans up to ₹5 Lakhs are offered at a highly concessional 5% interest rate. Loans from ₹5 Lakhs to ₹25 Lakhs are offered at 7%.

effective_interest_rate_note: A direct concessional soft loan at 5% (up to ₹5L) or 7% (up to ₹25L) per annum provided directly by KSIDC.
eligibility_human: Women entrepreneurs in Kerala looking to scale innovative, manufacturing, or service-oriented startups. The enterprise must be at least 51% owned by women.
pros: KSIDC directly finances the loan, avoiding commercial bank hurdles and collateral demands for smaller amounts.
1-year moratorium allows the business time to generate cash flow.
cons: Requires applicant to contribute 15% to 20% margin money depending on the loan tier.
application_steps: Register and submit the business plan online to KSIDC.
Attend the WE Mission screening and pitch session.
Upon approval, KSIDC sanctions and disburses the soft loan in milestone tranches.

name: Mukhyamantri Laghu Vanijyik Vahan Swarojgar Yojana
ministry: Industries Department, Govt of Rajasthan

manufacturer_discount.note: State provides 10% (max ₹60,000) and vehicle manufacturers (Tata, Mahindra, Ashok Leyland) provide a matching 10% discount, making the effective subsidy 20%.

effective_interest_rate_note: A margin money subsidy scheme to cover vehicle down payments. Standard commercial vehicle loan rates apply.
eligibility_human: Residents of Rajasthan aged 18 to 45 holding a valid driving license, wishing to buy a small commercial vehicle (up to ₹15 Lakh) for self-employment.
pros: Combines state grant with a mandatory manufacturer discount, knocking ~20% off the on-road price of a commercial vehicle.
Reduces or completely eliminates the down payment requirement.
cons: Scheme quota is capped (e.g., 3,300 vehicles per year) and operates on a first-come, first-served basis.
application_steps: Apply through the Rajasthan SSO portal selecting the preferred vehicle and dealer.
DIC conducts physical screening.
Bank finances the remaining 80%.
State transfers ₹60,000 margin directly to the dealer.

name: Mukhya Mantri Gramin Parivahan Yojana (Assam)
ministry: Transport Department, Govt of Assam
effective_interest_rate_note: A 25% direct margin money subsidy on commercial vehicles to improve rural connectivity.
eligibility_human: Unemployed youth in rural Assam aged 18+ who possess a valid commercial driving license and wish to operate a light commercial vehicle (LCV) for passenger or goods transport within their village.
pros: Provides up to ₹1 Lakh to offset the down payment of rural transport vehicles.
Generates direct self-employment while solving last-mile rural logistics.
cons: Permits are strictly issued for rural routes; operating the subsidized vehicle in city limits is prohibited.
application_steps: Submit application to the local DTO.
District Level Committee interviews candidates.
Bank sanctions 75% of the vehicle loan.
Transport department transfers 25% subsidy directly to the vehicle dealer.

name: Procurement and Marketing Support (PMS) Scheme
ministry: Ministry of Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises
